ambiguous_exact_statement_groups.statement: MAX_STREAMS frames that do not increase the stream limit MUST be ignored.
Packets containing a zero value for this bit are not valid packets in this version and MUST be discarded.
The Length field MUST be encoded as a variable-length integer.
The stateless reset token MUST be difficult to guess.
The value included prior to protection MUST be set to 0.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard connection state if it does not have a validated path on which it can send packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY discard connection state if it does not have a validated path on which it can send packets; see Section 8.2.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: To avoid excessively small idle timeout periods, endpoints MUST increase the idle timeout period to be at least three times the current Probe Timeout (PTO)
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To avoid excessively small idle timeout periods, endpoints MUST increase the idle timeout period to be at least three times the current Probe Timeout (PTO).

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Silently close on idle timeout
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If a max_idle_timeout is specified by either endpoint in its transport parameters, the connection MUST be silently closed and its state discarded when it remains idle for longer than the minimum of the max_idle_timeout values advertised by both endpoints.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Advertise and compute idle timeout
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Each endpoint MUST advertise a `max_idle_timeout`, and the effective value at an endpoint is the minimum of the two advertised values, or the sole advertised value if only one endpoint advertises a non-zero value.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Commit to immediate close before timeout
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that announces a max_idle_timeout MUST initiate an immediate close if it abandons the connection before the effective timeout expires.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Restart idle timer on fresh ack-eliciting send
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST also restart its idle timer when it sends an ack-eliciting packet if no other ack-eliciting packets have been sent since it last received and processed a packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow liveness probes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY send a PING or another ack-eliciting frame to test the connection for liveness if the peer could time out soon.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow deferring idle timeout
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An implementation of QUIC MAY provide applications with an option to defer an idle timeout.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: These states SHOULD persist for at least three times the current PTO interval as defined in [QUIC-RECOVERY]
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: These states SHOULD persist for at least three times the current PTO interval as defined in [QUIC-RECOVERY].

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: That have some alternative means to ensure that late-arriving packets do not induce a response, such as those that are able to close the UDP socket, MAY end these states earlier to allow for faster resource recovery
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints that have some alternative means to ensure that late-arriving packets do not induce a response, such as those that are able to close the UDP socket, MAY end these states earlier to allow for faster resource recovery.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Close all streams on CONNECTION_CLOSE
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MUST cause all streams to immediately become closed.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Reset open streams implicitly
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Open streams MUST be implicitly reset when a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame is sent.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter draining state after receiving close
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: After receiving a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, endpoints MUST enter the draining state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Close immediately on protocol violation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Violations of the protocol MUST lead to an immediate close.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Permit immediate close after application shutdown
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An immediate close MAY be used after an application protocol has arranged to close a connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: An endpoint's selected connection ID and the QUIC version are sufficient information to identify packets for a closing connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint's selected connection ID and the QUIC version are sufficient information to identify packets for a closing connection; the endpoint MAY discard all other connection state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: To avoid being used for an amplification attack, such endpoints MUST limit the cumulative size of packets it sends to three times the cumulative size of the packets that are received and attributed to the connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To avoid being used for an amplification attack, such endpoints MUST limit the cumulative size of packets it sends to three times the cumulative size of the packets that are received and attributed to the connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: To minimize the state that an endpoint maintains for a closing connection, endpoints MAY send the exact same packet in response to any received packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To minimize the state that an endpoint maintains for a closing connection, endpoints MAY send the exact same packet in response to any received packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Retain only closing-state essentials
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In the closing state, an endpoint MUST retain only enough information to generate a packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame and to identify packets as belonging to the connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: While otherwise identical to the closing state, an endpoint in the draining state MUST NOT send any packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: While otherwise identical to the closing state, an endpoint in the draining state MUST NOT send any packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: That receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY send a single packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame before entering the draining state, using a NO_ERROR code if appropriate
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY send a single packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame before entering the draining state, using a NO_ERROR code if appropriate.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send further packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send further packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter the draining state from the closing state if it receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, which indicates that the peer is also closing or draining
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY enter the draining state from the closing state if it receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, which indicates that the peer is also closing or draining.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter draining on peer close
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The draining state MUST be entered once an endpoint receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, which indicates that its peer is closing or draining.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: After the handshake is confirmed (see Section 4
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: After the handshake is confirmed (see Section 4.1.2 of [QUIC-TLS]), an endpoint MUST send any CONNECTION_CLOSE frames in a 1-RTT packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: However, prior to confirming the handshake, it is possible that more advanced packet protection keys are not available to the peer, so another CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY be sent in a packet that uses a lower packet protection level
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: However, prior to confirming the handshake, it is possible that more advanced packet protection keys are not available to the peer, so another CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY be sent in a packet that uses a lower packet protection level.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Under these circumstances, a server SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and Initial packets to ensure that at least one of them is processable by the client
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Under these circumstances, a server SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and Initial packets to ensure that at least one of them is processable by the client.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Prior to confirming the handshake, a peer might be unable to process 1-RTT packets, so an endpoint SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and 1-RTT packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Prior to confirming the handshake, a peer might be unable to process 1-RTT packets, so an endpoint SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and 1-RTT packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Also send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in an Initial packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A server SHOULD also send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in an Initial packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: For this reason, endpoints MAY discard packets rather than immediately close if errors are detected in packets that lack authentication
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: For this reason, endpoints MAY discard packets rather than immediately close if errors are detected in packets that lack authentication.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send post-handshake close in 1-RTT
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: After the handshake is confirmed, an endpoint MUST send any CONNECTION_CLOSE frames in a 1-RTT packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow lower-protection close before handshake confirmation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Prior to confirming the handshake, another CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY be sent in a packet that uses a lower packet protection level.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Close in Handshake and 1-RTT before confirmation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Prior to confirming the handshake, an endpoint SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and 1-RTT packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Downgrade close type for Initial and Handshake
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A CONNECTION_CLOSE frame of type 0x1d MUST be replaced by a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame of type 0x1c when sending the frame in Initial or Handshake packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Clear Reason Phrase when downgrading close type
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints MUST clear the value of the Reason Phrase field when converting to a CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1c.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Prefer APPLICATION_ERROR when downgrading close type
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints SHOULD use the APPLICATION_ERROR code when converting to a CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1c.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send a Stateless Reset in response to receiving a packet that it cannot associate with an active connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to receiving a packet that it cannot associate with an active connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use a hard-to-guess 16-byte stateless reset token
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A stateless reset token MUST be 16 bytes long and difficult to guess.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use the Figure 10 packet layout for Stateless Reset
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that receives packets that it cannot process MUST send a packet in the layout shown in Figure 10.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send Stateless Reset as a short-header packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A Stateless Reset MUST use an entire UDP datagram, starting with the first two bits of the packet header.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The remainder of the first byte and an arbitrary number of bytes following it are set to values that SHOULD be indistinguishable from random
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The remainder of the first byte and an arbitrary number of bytes following it are set to values that SHOULD be indistinguishable from random.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Include at least 38 unpredictable bits
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: For the Stateless Reset to appear as a valid QUIC packet, the Unpredictable Bits field MUST include at least 38 bits of data.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Pad packets to keep Stateless Reset hard to distinguish
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To achieve that end, the endpoint SHOULD ensure that all packets it sends are at least 22 bytes longer than the minimum connection ID length that it requests the peer to include in its packets, adding PADDING frames as necessary.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Make short-packet Stateless Resets one byte shorter
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that sends a Stateless Reset in response to a packet that is 43 bytes or shorter SHOULD send a Stateless Reset that is one byte shorter than the packet it responds to.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Format Stateless Resets with a short header
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints MUST send Stateless Resets formatted as a packet with a short header.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat any packet ending in a valid reset token as a Stateless Reset
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints MUST treat any packet ending in a valid stateless reset token as a Stateless Reset.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow Stateless Reset in response to long-header packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to a packet with a long header.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Make reset tokens hard to guess
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The stateless reset token MUST be difficult to guess.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Advertise reset tokens in NEW_CONNECTION_ID
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST issue a stateless reset token by including the value in the Stateless Reset Token field of a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Permit server transport-parameter reset tokens
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Servers MAY issue a stateless_reset_token transport parameter during the handshake that applies to the connection ID that it selected during the handshake.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: End the connection on received reset
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If a peer receives a Stateless Reset, it MUST immediately end the connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send reset using the Figure 10 layout
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that receives packets it cannot process MUST send a packet using the Stateless Reset layout shown in Figure 10.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Set fixed bits to 1
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Stateless Reset packets MUST set the fixed bits to 1.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Make leading reset bytes look random
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The remainder of the first byte and an arbitrary number of bytes following it SHOULD be indistinguishable from random.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Place the token in the tail
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The last 16 bytes of a Stateless Reset datagram MUST contain a stateless reset token.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Provide enough unpredictable bits
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The Unpredictable Bits field MUST include at least 38 bits of data.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use a full UDP datagram
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A Stateless Reset MUST use an entire UDP datagram starting with the first two bits of the packet header.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Pad packets to improve reset indistinguishability
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To achieve that end, the endpoint SHOULD ensure that all packets it sends are at least 22 bytes longer than the minimum connection ID length it requests the peer to include in its packets, adding PADDING frames as necessary.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Avoid amplification with Stateless Reset
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send a Stateless Reset that is three times or more larger than the packet it receives to avoid being used for amplification.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Support all negotiated versions in reset generation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that supports multiple versions of QUIC MUST generate a Stateless Reset that will be accepted by peers that support any version that the endpoint might support or might have supported prior to losing state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use the trailing 16 bytes to detect Stateless Reset
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST use the trailing 16 bytes of the UDP datagram to detect a potential Stateless Reset.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Remember recent stateless reset tokens
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST remember all stateless reset tokens associated with the connection IDs and remote addresses for datagrams it has recently sent.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Compare the remote-address token set to classify Stateless Reset
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST identify a received datagram as a Stateless Reset by comparing the last 16 bytes of the datagram with all stateless reset tokens associated with the remote address on which the datagram was received.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Skip the token check after successful packet processing
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints MAY skip this check if any packet from a datagram is successfully processed.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Always check when the first packet cannot be processed
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: However, the comparison MUST be performed when the first packet in an incoming datagram either cannot be associated with a connection or cannot be decrypted.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Ignore unused and retired reset tokens
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT check for any stateless reset tokens associated with connection IDs it has not used or for connection IDs that have been retired.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Avoid leaking token values during comparison
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When comparing a datagram to stateless reset token values, endpoints MUST perform the comparison without leaking information about the value of the token.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter draining on a matching stateless reset token
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the last 16 bytes of the datagram are identical in value to a stateless reset token, the endpoint MUST enter the draining period and not send any further packets on this connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Remember and scope reset tokens
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST remember all stateless reset tokens associated with connection IDs and remote addresses for datagrams it has recently sent, including Stateless Reset Token field values from NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames and the server's transport parameters, and excluding tokens associated with connection IDs that are unused or retired.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Be difficult to guess
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The stateless reset token MUST be difficult to guess.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Truncate the stateless reset token to 16 bytes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The output of this function MUST be truncated to 16 bytes to produce the stateless reset token for that connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use a recoverable connection ID length with static-key tokens
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that uses this design MUST either use the same connection ID length for all connections or encode the length of the connection ID such that it can be recovered without state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Disallow zero-length connection IDs for static-key tokens
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A static-key token function MUST NOT provide a zero-length connection ID.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not reuse the connection ID and static key combination
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: This method for choosing the stateless reset token means that the combination of connection ID and static key MUST NOT be used for another connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow duplicate stateless reset tokens to signal protocol violation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints are not required to compare new values against all previous values, but a duplicate value MAY be treated as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow per-connection random secrets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In order to create a stateless reset token, an endpoint MAY randomly generate a secret for every connection that it creates.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow static-key token generation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A single static key MAY be used across all connections to the same endpoint by generating the proof using a pseudorandom function that takes a static key and the connection ID chosen by the endpoint as input.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Forbid zero-length connection IDs
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that uses this design MUST NOT provide a zero-length connection ID.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Keep Stateless Reset smaller than the triggering packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST ensure that every Stateless Reset that it sends is smaller than the packet that triggered it, unless it maintains state sufficient to prevent looping.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow a reset-send limit
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY remember the number of Stateless Resets that it has sent and stop generating new Stateless Resets once a limit is reached.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: that detects an error SHOULD signal the existence of that error to its peer
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that detects an error SHOULD signal the existence of that error to its peer.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The most appropriate error code (Section 20) SHOULD be included in the frame that signals the error
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The most appropriate error code (Section 20) SHOULD be included in the frame that signals the error.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Errors that result in the connection being unusable, such as an obvious violation of protocol semantics or corruption of state that affects an entire connection, MUST be signaled using a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame (Section 19
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Errors that result in the connection being unusable, such as an obvious violation of protocol semantics or corruption of state that affects an entire connection, MUST be signaled using a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame (Section 19.19).

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use CONNECTION_CLOSE type 0x1c for transport errors
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Transport errors, including all those described in this document, MUST be carried in the CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with a frame type of 0x1c.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Limiting the number of retransmissions and the time over which this final packet is sent limits the effort expended on terminated connections
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Limiting the number of retransmissions and the time over which this final packet MUST be sent limits the effort expended on terminated connections.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: An endpoint that continues to receive data for a terminated connection MUST attempt the stateless reset process
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that continues to receive data for a terminated connection MUST attempt the stateless reset process (Section 10.3).

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: As the AEAD for Initial packets does not provide strong authentication, an endpoint MAY discard an invalid Initial packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: As the AEAD for Initial packets does not provide strong authentication, an endpoint MAY discard an invalid Initial packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: If an application-level error affects a single stream but otherwise leaves the connection in a recoverable state, the endpoint can send a RESET_STREAM frame (Section 19
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If an application-level error MUST affects a single stream but otherwise leaves the connection in a recoverable state, the endpoint can send a RESET_STREAM frame (Section 19.4) with an appropriate error code to terminate just the affected stream.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: RESET_STREAM MUST only be instigated by the application protocol that uses QUIC
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: RESET_STREAM MUST only be instigated by the application protocol that uses QUIC.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow stream termination only by the application protocol
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A stream MUST only be terminated by the application protocol.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: A local instance of the application protocol uses a direct API call, and a remote instance uses the STOP_SENDING frame, which triggers an automatic RESET_STREAM
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A local instance of MUST the application protocol uses a direct API call, and a remote instance uses the STOP_SENDING frame, which triggers an automatic RESET_STREAM.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Version Negotiation packets have no cryptographic protection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Version Negotiation packets MUST NOT have cryptographic protection; see [QUIC-INVARIANTS].

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Retry packets use an AEAD function [AEAD] to protect against accidental modification
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Retry packets use an MUST AEAD function [AEAD] to protect against accidental modification.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Initial packets use an AEAD function, the keys for which are derived using a value that is visible on the wire
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Initial packets use an MUST AEAD function, the keys for which are derived using a value that is visible on the wire.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Initial protection exists to ensure that the sender of the packet is on the network path
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Initial protection exists to MUST ensure that the sender of the packet is on the network path.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Any entity that receives an Initial packet from a client can recover the keys that will allow them to both read the contents of the packet and generate Initial packets that will be successfully authenticated at either endpoint
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Any entity that receives MUST an Initial packet from a client can recover the keys that will allow them to both read the contents of the packet and generate Initial packets that will be successfully authenticated at either endpoint.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The AEAD also protects Initial packets against accidental modification
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The AEAD also protects MUST Initial packets against accidental modification.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The cryptographic handshake ensures that only the communicating endpoints receive the corresponding keys for Handshake, 0-RTT, and 1-RTT packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The cryptographic handshake ensures MUST that only the communicating endpoints receive the corresponding keys for Handshake, 0-RTT, and 1-RTT packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The length includes both the Packet Number and Payload fields, both of which are confidentiality protected and initially of unknown length
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The length includes both MUST the Packet Number and Payload fields, both of which are confidentiality protected and initially of unknown length.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Using the Length field, a sender can coalesce multiple QUIC packets into one UDP datagram
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Using the Length MUST field, a sender can coalesce multiple QUIC packets into one UDP datagram.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: include multiple frames in a single packet if they are to be sent at the same encryption level, instead of coalescing multiple packets at the same encryption level
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint SHOULD include multiple frames in a single packet if they are to be sent at the same encryption level, instead of coalescing multiple packets at the same encryption level.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Buffer or discard on decryption failure
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If decryption fails, the receiver MAY either discard or buffer the packet for later processing.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Continue processing remaining coalesced packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If decryption fails, the receiver MUST attempt to process the remaining packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Process each coalesced packet separately
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The receiver of coalesced QUIC packets MUST individually process each QUIC packet and separately acknowledge each QUIC packet, as if the packets were received as the payload of different UDP datagrams.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Retry packets (Section 17
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Retry packets (Section 17.2.5), Version Negotiation packets (Section 17.2.1), and packets with a short header (Section 17.3) MUST NOT contain a Length field or be followed by other packets in the same UDP datagram.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: This number is used in determining the cryptographic nonce for packet protection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: This number MUST be used in determining the cryptographic nonce for packet protection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: maintains a separate packet number for sending and receiving
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Each endpoint maintains a MUST separate packet number for sending and receiving.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Version Negotiation (Section 17
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Version Negotiation (Section 17.2.1) and Retry (Section 17.2.5) packets MUST NOT include a packet number.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Initial packets can only be sent with Initial packet protection keys and acknowledged in packets that are also Initial packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Initial packets MUST only be sent with Initial packet protection keys and acknowledged in packets that are also Initial packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Similarly, Handshake packets are sent at the Handshake encryption level and can only be acknowledged in Handshake packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Handshake packets MUST be sent at the Handshake encryption level and be acknowledged only in Handshake packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: numbers in each space start at packet number 0
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packet numbers in each MUST space start at packet number 0.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow Stateless Reset after packet-number exhaustion
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to further packets that it receives after packet-number exhaustion.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Duplicate suppression MUST happen after removing packet protection for the reasons described in Section 9
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Duplicate suppression MUST happen after removing packet protection for the reasons described in Section 9.5 of [QUIC-TLS].

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Keep frames within one packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Frames MUST fit within a single QUIC packet rather than span multiple packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: A description of this summary is included after the table
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A description of this summary MUST be included after the table.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use Frame Type for frame-specific flags in selected frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The Frame Type in ACK, STREAM, MAX_STREAMS, STREAMS_BLOCKED, and CONNECTION_CLOSE frames MUST be used to carry other frame-specific flags.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Limit Initial and Handshake appearance of CONNECTION_CLOSE type 0x1c
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Only a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame of type 0x1c MAY appear in Initial or Handshake packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat N-marked packets as not ack-eliciting
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets containing only frames with the N marking MUST NOT be ack-eliciting.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Exclude C-marked packets from bytes in flight
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets containing only frames with the C marking MUST NOT count toward bytes in flight for congestion control purposes.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow P-marked packets to probe new paths
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets containing only frames with the P marking MAY be used to probe new network paths during connection migration.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat F-marked frame contents as flow controlled
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The contents of frames with the F marking MUST be flow controlled.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat unknown frame types as frame encoding errors
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a frame of unknown type as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Make frames idempotent
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: All frames MUST be idempotent in this version of QUIC.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: That is, a valid frame does not cause undesirable side effects or errors when received more than once
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: That is, a valid frame MUST NOT cause undesirable side effects or errors when received more than once.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow longer-than-necessary frame-type encodings to fail
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY treat receipt of a frame type that uses a longer encoding than necessary as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The rules here generalize those of TLS, in that frames associated with establishing the connection can usually appear in packets in any packet number space, whereas those associated with transferring data can only appear in the application data packet number space
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The rules here generalize those of TLS, in that frames associated with establishing the connection can usually appear in packets in any packet number space, whereas those associated with transferring data MUST only appear in the application data packet number space:

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow QUIC-layer CONNECTION_CLOSE in any packet number space
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: CONNECTION_CLOSE frames signaling errors at the QUIC layer MAY appear in any packet number space.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Restrict application-error CONNECTION_CLOSE to application data
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: CONNECTION_CLOSE frames signaling application errors MUST only appear in the application data packet number space.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow ACK in any packet number space but only acknowledge within that space
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: ACK frames MAY appear in any packet number space, but they can only acknowledge packets that appeared in that packet number space.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: treat receipt of these frames in 0-RTT packets as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A server MAY treat receipt of these frames in 0-RTT packets as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send one or more frames in each QUIC packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A sender MUST send one or more frames in a QUIC packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: wait for a short period of time to collect multiple frames before sending a packet that is not maximally packed, to avoid sending out large numbers of small packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A sender MAY wait for a short period of time to collect multiple frames before sending a packet that is not maximally packed, to avoid sending out large numbers of small packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: An implementation MAY use knowledge about application sending behavior or heuristics to determine whether and for how long to wait
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An implementation MAY use knowledge about application sending behavior or heuristics to determine whether and for how long to wait.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: A single QUIC packet can include multiple STREAM frames from one or more streams
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY include multiple STREAM frames from one or more streams in a single QUIC packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Implementations are advised to include as few streams as necessary in outgoing packets without losing transmission efficiency to underfilled packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Implementations SHOULD include as few streams as necessary in outgoing packets without losing transmission efficiency to underfilled packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: For STREAM frames, this means the data has been enqueued in preparation to be received by the application protocol, but it does not require that data be delivered and consumed
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: For STREAM frames, this means the data has been enqueued in preparation to be received by the application protocol, but it MUST NOT require that data be delivered and consumed.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Acknowledge processed packets with ACK frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Once the packet has been fully processed, a receiver MUST acknowledge receipt by sending one or more ACK frames containing the packet number of the received packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send ACK frames within max_ack_delay only for ack-eliciting packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Only ack-eliciting packets MUST cause an ACK frame to be sent within the maximum ack delay.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Acknowledge non-ack-eliciting packets only for other reasons
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets that are not ack-eliciting MUST only be acknowledged when an ACK frame is sent for other reasons.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Acknowledge ack-eliciting packets within max_ack_delay
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Ack-eliciting packets MUST be acknowledged at least once within the maximum delay the endpoint communicated using the max_ack_delay transport parameter.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: uses the receiver's max_ack_delay value in determining timeouts for timer-based retransmission, as detailed in Section 6
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A sender uses the MUST receiver's max_ack_delay value in determining timeouts for timer-based retransmission, as detailed in Section 6.2 of [QUIC-RECOVERY].

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Acknowledge 0-RTT and 1-RTT packets within max_ack_delay
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST acknowledge all ack-eliciting 0-RTT and 1-RTT packets within its advertised max_ack_delay.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Acknowledge Initial and Handshake packets immediately
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST acknowledge all ack-eliciting Initial and Handshake packets immediately.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not send multiple ACK-only packets in response to one ack-eliciting packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Since packets containing only ACK frames are not congestion controlled, an endpoint MUST NOT send more than one such packet in response to receiving an ack-eliciting packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not send non-ack-eliciting packets in response to non-ack-eliciting packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send a non-ack-eliciting packet in response to a non-ack-eliciting packet, even if there are packet gaps that precede the received packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Non-ack-eliciting packets are eventually acknowledged when the endpoint sends an ACK frame in response to other events
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Non-ack-eliciting packets are eventually MUST acknowledged when the endpoint sends an ACK frame in response to other events.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Avoid relying on ACK-only packets to elicit acknowledgments
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT rely on ACK-only packets to elicit acknowledgments from its peer.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Avoid infinite feedback loops when adding ack-eliciting frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In that case, an endpoint MUST NOT send an ack-eliciting frame in all packets that would otherwise be non-ack-eliciting.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send ACK frames without delay for out-of-order or gap-detecting packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To assist loss detection at the sender, an endpoint SHOULD generate and send an ACK frame without delay when it receives an ack-eliciting packet that has a packet number less than another ack-eliciting packet that has been received, or when the packet has a packet number larger than the highest-numbered ack-eliciting packet that has been received and there are missing packets between that packet and this packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: determines how frequently to send acknowledgments in response to ack-eliciting packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A receiver determines how MUST frequently to send acknowledgments in response to ack-eliciting packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: When an ACK frame is sent, one or more ranges of acknowledged packets are included
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When an ACK frame is sent, one or more ranges of acknowledged packets MUST be included.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: If it does not, then older ranges (those with the smallest packet numbers) are omitted
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If it MUST NOT, then older ranges (those with the smallest packet numbers) are omitted.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Senders can expect acknowledgments for most packets, but QUIC does not guarantee receipt of an acknowledgment for every packet that the receiver processes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Senders can expect acknowledgments for most packets, but QUIC MUST NOT guarantee receipt of an acknowledgment for every packet that the receiver processes.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard ACK ranges when a frame would be too large
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A receiver MUST discard unacknowledged ACK Ranges if an ACK frame would be too large to fit in a packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Retain the largest successfully processed packet number
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Receivers MAY discard all ACK Ranges if they retain the largest packet number that has been successfully processed.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Section 13
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Section MUST 13.2.4 describes an exemplary approach for determining what packets to acknowledge in each ACK frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: In cases with ACK frame loss and reordering, this approach does not guarantee that every acknowledgment is seen by the sender before it is no longer included in the ACK frame
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In cases with ACK frame loss and reordering, this approach MUST NOT guarantee that every acknowledgment is seen by the sender before it is no longer included in the ACK frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Measure intentional acknowledgment delays
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST measure the delays intentionally introduced between the time the packet with the largest packet number is received and the time an acknowledgment is sent.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Encode acknowledgment delay in ACK Delay
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The endpoint MUST encode this acknowledgment delay in the ACK Delay field of an ACK frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Report measured delay when it exceeds max_ack_delay
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When the measured acknowledgment delay is larger than its max_ack_delay, an endpoint SHOULD report the measured delay.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Carry ACK frames only in the same packet number space
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: ACK frames MUST only be carried in a packet that has the same packet number space as the packet being acknowledged.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use 1-RTT for acknowledging 1-RTT packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets that are protected with 1-RTT keys MUST be acknowledged in packets that are also protected with 1-RTT keys.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Acknowledge client 0-RTT packets with 1-RTT packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets that a client sends with 0-RTT packet protection MUST be acknowledged by the server in packets protected by 1-RTT keys.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: This can mean that the client is unable to use these acknowledgments if the server cryptographic handshake messages are delayed or lost
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client MAY be unable to use 0-RTT acknowledgments when the server cryptographic handshake messages are delayed or lost.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send non-PADDING frames periodically to elicit acknowledgments
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To avoid a deadlock, a sender SHOULD ensure that other frames are sent periodically in addition to PADDING frames to elicit acknowledgments from the receiver.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not retransmit lost packets whole
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: QUIC packets that are determined to be lost MUST NOT be retransmitted whole.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not retransmit lost frames whole
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The same rule MUST apply to the frames that are contained within lost packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send lost information again in new frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Instead, the information that might be carried in frames MUST be sent again in new frames as needed.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use new frames and packets for lost information
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: New frames and packets MUST be used to carry information that is determined to have been lost.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Stop resending information once it is acknowledged
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In general, information MUST be sent again when a packet containing that information is determined to be lost and cease being sent when a packet containing that information is acknowledged.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard CRYPTO data when its packet number space is discarded
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Data in CRYPTO frames for Initial and Handshake packets MUST be discarded when the keys for the corresponding packet number space are discarded.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Retransmit STREAM data unless RESET_STREAM was sent
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Application data sent in STREAM frames MUST be retransmitted in new STREAM frames unless the endpoint has sent a RESET_STREAM for that stream.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Stop needing STREAM frames after RESET_STREAM
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Once an endpoint sends a RESET_STREAM frame, it MAY omit further STREAM frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Carry the most recent acknowledgments and delay in ACK frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: ACK frames MUST carry the most recent set of acknowledgments and the acknowledgment delay from the largest acknowledged packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Retransmit RESET_STREAM until acknowledged or data is acknowledged
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Cancellation of stream transmission, as carried in a RESET_STREAM frame, MUST be sent until acknowledged or until all stream data is acknowledged by the peer.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Retransmit STOP_SENDING until the stream reaches a terminal state
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A request to cancel stream transmission, as encoded in a STOP_SENDING frame, MUST be sent until the receiving part of the stream enters either a Data Recvd state or a Reset Recvd state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send current connection maximum data in MAX_DATA frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The current connection maximum data MUST be sent in MAX_DATA frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send current stream data offsets in MAX_STREAM_DATA frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The current maximum stream data offset MUST be sent in MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send updated MAX_STREAM_DATA values when the frame is lost or the limit changes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Like MAX_DATA, an updated value MUST be sent when the packet containing the most recent MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a stream is lost or when the limit is updated.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Stop sending MAX_STREAM_DATA once the stream is closed or reset
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint SHOULD stop sending MAX_STREAM_DATA frames when the receiving part of the stream enters a Size Known or Reset Recvd state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send updated MAX_STREAMS values when the frame is lost or the limit changes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Like MAX_DATA, an updated value MUST be sent when a packet containing the most recent MAX_STREAMS for a stream type frame is declared lost or when the limit is updated.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Carry blocked signals in dedicated frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Blocked signals MUST be carried in DATA_BLOCKED, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, and STREAMS_BLOCKED frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Scope blocked signals appropriately
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: DATA_BLOCKED, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, and STREAMS_BLOCKED frames MUST use connection, stream, and stream-type scope respectively.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send a new blocked frame while blocked and the latest frame is lost
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A new frame MUST be sent if a packet containing the most recent frame for a scope is lost, but only while the endpoint is blocked on the corresponding limit.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Include the blocking limit in blocked frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: These frames MUST always include the limit that is causing blocking at the time that they are transmitted.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send new connection IDs in NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames and retransmit them if lost
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: New connection IDs MUST be sent in NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames and retransmitted if the packet containing them is lost.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send retired connection IDs in RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames and retransmit them if lost
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Retired connection IDs MUST be sent in RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames and retransmitted if the packet containing them is lost.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Compare NEW_TOKEN frames directly for duplicates and reordering
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: No special support MUST be used for detecting reordered and duplicated NEW_TOKEN frames other than a direct comparison of the frame contents.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: PING and PADDING frames contain no information, so lost PING or PADDING frames do not require repair
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: PING and PADDING frames contain no information, so lost PING or PADDING frames MUST NOT require repair.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: prioritize retransmission of data over sending new data, unless priorities specified by the application indicate otherwise
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints SHOULD prioritize retransmission of data over sending new data, unless priorities specified by the application indicate otherwise; see Section 2.3.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: This includes packets that are acknowledged after being declared lost, which can happen in the presence of network reordering
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: This includes packets that MUST are acknowledged after being declared lost, which can happen in the presence of network reordering.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: can discard this information after a period of time elapses that adequately allows for reordering, such as a PTO (Section 6
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A sender can discard MUST this information after a period of time elapses that adequately allows for reordering, such as a PTO (Section 6.2 of [QUIC-RECOVERY]), or based on other events, such as reaching a memory limit.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: QUIC endpoints MAY use ECN to detect and respond to network congestion
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: QUIC endpoints MAY use ECN [RFC3168] to detect and respond to network congestion.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Check whether the path and peer support ECN before enabling it
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To enable ECN, a sending QUIC endpoint MUST first determine whether a path supports ECN marking and whether the peer reports the ECN values in received IP headers.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not report ECN counts without ECN support or ECN field access
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If an endpoint does not implement ECN support or does not have access to received ECN fields, it MUST NOT report ECN counts for packets it receives.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Even if an endpoint does not set an ECT field in packets it sends, the endpoint MUST provide feedback about ECN markings it receives, if these are accessible
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Even if an endpoint does not set an ECT field in packets it sends, the endpoint MUST provide feedback about ECN markings it receives, if these are accessible.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Failing to report the ECN counts will cause the sender to disable the use of ECN for this connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Failing to report the MUST ECN counts will cause the sender to disable the use of ECN for this connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Update ECN counts when receiving marked IP packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: On receiving an IP packet with an ECT(0), ECT(1), or ECN-CE codepoint, an ECN-enabled endpoint MUST access the ECN field and increase the corresponding ECT(0), ECT(1), or ECN-CE count.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Include ECN counts in subsequent ACK frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: These ECN counts MUST be included in subsequent ACK frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Keep separate ECN counts per packet number space
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Each packet number space MUST maintain separate acknowledgment state and separate ECN counts.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Count ECN once per coalesced QUIC packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Coalesced QUIC packets share the same IP header so the ECN counts MUST be incremented once for each coalesced QUIC packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Count ECN for each packet number space in a coalesced datagram
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If one Initial, one Handshake, and one 1-RTT QUIC packet are coalesced into a single UDP datagram, the ECN counts for all three packet number spaces MUST be incremented by one each based on the ECN field of the single IP header.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Validate ECN counts per path and disable ECN on errors
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To ensure connectivity in the presence of such devices, an endpoint MUST validate the ECN counts for each network path and disable the use of ECN on that path if errors are detected.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Watch for ECN-marked packets being lost
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The endpoint MUST monitor whether all packets sent with an ECT codepoint are eventually deemed lost, indicating that ECN validation has failed.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Validate ECN for each new connection and path change
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST attempt to use ECN and validate this for each new connection, when switching to a server's preferred address, and on active connection migration to a new path.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Implementations MAY use other methods defined in RFCs
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Implementations MAY use other methods defined in RFCs; see [RFC8311].

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Validate ECN using ECT(1) counts when ECT(1) is used
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Implementations that use the ECT(1) codepoint MUST perform ECN validation using the reported ECT(1) counts.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Validate ECN counts before using them
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that receives an ACK frame with ECN counts MUST validate the counts before using them.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Fail ECN validation when counts are missing for newly acknowledged ECT packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If an ACK frame newly acknowledges a packet that the endpoint sent with either the ECT(0) or ECT(1) codepoint set, ECN validation MUST fail if the corresponding ECN counts are not present in the ACK frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: This check detects a network element that zeroes the ECN field or a peer that does not report ECN markings
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: This check detects a network element that zeroes the ECN field or a peer that MUST NOT report ECN markings.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Fail ECN validation when ECT(0) and CE counts are too small
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: ECN validation MUST fail if the sum of the increase in ECT(0) and ECN-CE counts is less than the number of newly acknowledged packets that were originally sent with an ECT(0) marking.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Fail ECN validation when ECT(1) and CE counts are too small
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: ECN validation MUST fail if the sum of the increases to ECT(1) and ECN-CE counts is less than the number of newly acknowledged packets sent with an ECT(1) marking.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Fail ECN validation when received counts exceed sent counts
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: ECN validation MUST fail if the received total count for either ECT(0) or ECT(1) exceeds the total number of packets sent with each corresponding ECT codepoint.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Fail ECN validation for never-applied ECT counts
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Validation MUST fail when an endpoint receives a non-zero ECN count corresponding to an ECT codepoint that it never applied.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Disable ECN when validation fails
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If validation fails, then the endpoint MUST disable ECN.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: It stops setting the ECT codepoint in IP packets that it sends, assuming that either the network path or the peer does not support ECN
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: It stops setting the ECT codepoint in IP packets that it sends, assuming that either the network path or the peer MUST NOT support ECN.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Even if validation fails, an endpoint MAY revalidate ECN for the same path at any later time in the connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Even if validation fails, an endpoint MAY revalidate ECN for the same path at any later time in the connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Upon successful validation, an endpoint MAY continue to set an ECT codepoint in subsequent packets it sends, with the expectation that the path is ECN capable
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Upon successful validation, an endpoint MAY continue to set an ECT codepoint in subsequent packets it sends, with the expectation that the path is ECN capable.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Network routing and path elements can change mid-connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Network routing and path elements can change mid-connection; an endpoint MUST disable ECN if validation later fails.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The datagram size includes one or more QUIC packet headers and protected payloads, but not the UDP or IP headers
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The datagram size includes MUST one or more QUIC packet headers and protected payloads, but not the UDP or IP headers.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Define maximum datagram size as the largest UDP payload across a path
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The maximum datagram size MUST be defined as the largest size of UDP payload that can be sent across a network path using a single UDP datagram.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use PMTUD or DPLPMTUD to discover larger datagram sizes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Any maximum datagram size larger than 1200 bytes MUST be discovered using Path Maximum Transmission Unit Discovery (PMTUD) or Datagram Packetization Layer PMTU Discovery (DPLPMTUD).

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Avoid exceeding the max_udp_payload_size once known
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A sender MUST avoid exceeding the max_udp_payload_size transport parameter limit once the value is known.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: In IPv4 [IPv4], the Don't Fragment (DF) bit MUST be set if possible, to prevent fragmentation on the path
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In IPv4 [IPv4], the Don't Fragment (DF) bit MUST be set if possible, to prevent fragmentation on the path.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat received datagram size as unauthenticated
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If an endpoint receives a datagram of a certain size, it MUST NOT assume that the sender sent the datagram at the same size.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Pad Initial datagrams to 1200 bytes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client MUST expand the payload of all UDP datagrams carrying Initial packets to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes by adding PADDING frames to the Initial packet or by coalescing the Initial packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Initial packets can even be coalesced with invalid packets, which a receiver will discard
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Initial packets can even MUST be coalesced with invalid packets, which a receiver will discard.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Pad server Initial datagrams to 1200 bytes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A server MUST expand the payload of all UDP datagrams carrying ack-eliciting Initial packets to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Sending UDP datagrams of this size ensures that the network path supports a reasonable Path Maximum Transmission Unit (PMTU), in both directions
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Sending UDP datagrams of MUST this size ensures that the network path supports a reasonable Path Maximum Transmission Unit (PMTU), in both directions.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow oversized Initial datagrams when the path and peer support them
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Datagrams containing Initial packets MAY exceed 1200 bytes if the sender believes that the network path and peer both support the size that it chooses.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard undersized Initial packets at the server
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A server MUST discard an Initial packet that is carried in a UDP datagram with a payload that is smaller than the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow servers to close on undersized Initial packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A server MAY also immediately close the connection by sending a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with an error code of PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Limit bytes sent before validating the client address
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The server MUST also limit the number of bytes it sends before validating the address of the client.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The UDP payload includes one or more QUIC packet headers and protected payloads
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The UDP payload includes MUST one or more QUIC packet headers and protected payloads.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The largest UDP payload an endpoint sends at any given time is referred to as the endpoint's maximum datagram size
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The largest UDP payload MUST an endpoint sends at any given time is referred to as the endpoint's maximum datagram size.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use DPLPMTUD or PMTUD to determine support for a desired size
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint SHOULD use DPLPMTUD or PMTUD to determine whether the path to a destination will support a desired maximum datagram size without fragmentation.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not exceed the smallest allowed maximum datagram size without PMTU discovery
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In the absence of these mechanisms, QUIC endpoints SHOULD NOT send datagrams larger than the smallest allowed maximum datagram size.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Both DPLPMTUD and PMTUD send datagrams that are larger than the current maximum datagram size, referred to as PMTU probes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Both DPLPMTUD and PMTUD MUST send datagrams that are larger than the current maximum datagram size, referred to as PMTU probes.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Size non-PMTU-probe packets to fit within the maximum datagram size
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: All QUIC packets that are not sent in a PMTU probe SHOULD be sized to fit within the maximum datagram size.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Stop sending packets on a path that cannot support 1200 bytes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If a QUIC endpoint determines that the PMTU between any pair of local and remote IP addresses cannot support the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes, it MUST immediately cease sending QUIC packets on the affected path except for those in PMTU probes or those containing CONNECTION_CLOSE frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Maintain a maximum datagram size per address pair when doing PMTU discovery
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: QUIC implementations that implement any kind of PMTU discovery SHOULD maintain a maximum datagram size for each combination of local and remote IP addresses.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow conservative maximum datagram size estimates
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A QUIC implementation MAY be more conservative in computing the maximum datagram size to allow for unknown tunnel overheads or IP header options or extensions.

live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: QUIC endpoints implementing DPLPMTUD MUST maintain a DPLPMTUD Maximum Packet Size for each combination of local and remote IP addresses.

live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: PMTU probes MUST be ack-eliciting packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not treat PMTU probe loss as congestion
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Loss of a QUIC packet that is carried in a PMTU probe SHOULD NOT trigger a congestion control reaction.

live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The use of the first unassigned codepoint MUST be reserved for allocation using the Standards Action policy.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow early codepoint assignment for selected values
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The early codepoint assignment process MAY be used for these values.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: For codepoints that are encoded in variable-length integers (Section 16), such as frame types...
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: For codepoints that are encoded in variable-length integers (Section 16), such as frame types, codepoints that encode to four or eight bytes (that is, values 214 and above) SHOULD be used unless the usage is especially sensitive to having a longer encoding.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: IANA MUST allocate the selected codepoint if the codepoint is unassigned and the requirements...
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: IANA MUST allocate the selected codepoint if the codepoint is unassigned and the requirements of the registration policy are met.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use Specification Required for permanent registrations
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Permanent registrations in QUIC registries MUST use the Specification Required policy (Section 4.6 of [RFC8126]), unless otherwise specified.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Verify the specification for permanent registrations
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The designated expert or experts MUST verify that a specification exists and is readily accessible.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The creation of a registry MAY specify additional constraints on permanent registrations
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The creation of a registry MAY specify additional constraints on permanent registrations.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The creation of a registry MAY identify a range of codepoints where registrations are governe...
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The creation of a registry MAY identify a range of codepoints where registrations are governed by a different registration policy.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not block provisional registrations with stricter permanent requirements
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Any stricter requirements for permanent registrations MUST NOT prevent provisional registrations for affected codepoints.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Assign document registrations permanent status
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: All registrations in this document MUST be assigned a permanent status.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Record the change controller and contact for document registrations
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: All registrations in this document MUST list a change controller of the IETF and a contact of the QUIC Working Group (quic@ietf.org).

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Assign codepoint 0x00000001
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The codepoint of 0x00000001 for the protocol MUST be assigned with permanent status to the protocol defined in this document.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Exclude reserved version-pattern codepoints from listings
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: All codepoints that follow the pattern 0x?a?a?a?a MUST NOT appear in the listing of assigned values.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Protect reserved version-pattern codepoints
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: All codepoints that follow the pattern 0x?a?a?a?a MUST NOT be assigned by IANA.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use Specification Required for transport parameters
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST be assigned using the Specification Required policy.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use stricter policy for low transport-parameter codepoints
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Values between 0x00 and 0x3f inclusive MUST be assigned using Standards Action or IESG Approval.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Include Parameter Name for transport parameters
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST include the Parameter Name field.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Define Parameter Name
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The Parameter Name field MUST be a short mnemonic for the parameter.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use Specification Required for frame types
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST be assigned using the Specification Required policy.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use stricter policy for low frame-type codepoints
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Values between 0x00 and 0x3f inclusive MUST be assigned using Standards Action or IESG Approval.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Include Frame Type Name for frame types
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST include the Frame Type Name field.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Define Frame Type Name
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The Frame Type Name field MUST be a short mnemonic for the frame type.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: In addition to the advice in Section 22.1, specifications for new permanent registrations SHO...
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In addition to the advice in Section 22.1, specifications for new permanent registrations SHOULD describe the means by which an endpoint might determine that it can send the identified type of frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Describe frame field semantics in specifications
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Specifications for permanent registrations MUST describe the format and assigned semantics of any fields in the frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use Specification Required for transport error codes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST be assigned using the Specification Required policy.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use stricter policy for low transport error codepoints
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Values between 0x00 and 0x3f inclusive MUST be assigned using Standards Action or IESG Approval.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Include Code and Description for transport error codes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST include the following fields.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Define Code
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The Code field MUST be a short mnemonic for the parameter.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Define Description
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The Description field MUST be a brief description of the error code semantics.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Constrain unidirectional stream direction
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A unidirectional stream MUST carry data only from the initiator of the stream to its peer.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Constrain bidirectional stream direction
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A bidirectional stream MUST allow data to be sent in both directions.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Identify streams by stream ID
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Each stream MUST be identified within a connection by a numeric value called the stream ID.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use the low bit to identify stream initiator
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The least significant bit of a stream ID MUST identify the initiator of the stream.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use even IDs for client-initiated streams
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Client-initiated streams MUST have even-numbered stream IDs with the least significant bit set to 0.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use odd IDs for server-initiated streams
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Server-initiated streams MUST have odd-numbered stream IDs with the least significant bit set to 1.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use the second low bit to distinguish stream direction
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The second least significant bit of a stream ID MUST distinguish bidirectional streams from unidirectional streams, with 0 indicating bidirectional and 1 indicating unidirectional.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Start each stream space at its minimum value
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The stream space for each type MUST begin at its minimum value.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Open lower-numbered streams when a stream ID is used out of order
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Using a stream ID out of order MUST cause all lower-numbered streams of that type to be opened.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Encapsulate application data in STREAM frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: STREAM frames MUST encapsulate data sent by an application.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Buffer out-of-order stream data until it can be delivered in order
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To deliver an ordered byte stream, an endpoint MUST buffer any out-of-order data it receives up to the advertised flow control limit.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow optional out-of-order delivery to applications
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Implementations MAY offer the ability to deliver stream data out of order to a receiving application.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Permit discarded received data
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY discard data that has already been received.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Keep retransmitted stream data stable at the same offset
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The data at a given offset MUST NOT change if it is sent multiple times.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Expose streams as ordered byte streams only
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Streams MUST be an ordered byte-stream abstraction with no other structure visible to QUIC.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Avoid a built-in prioritization exchange
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: QUIC MUST NOT provide a mechanism for exchanging prioritization information.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use application priority information for resource allocation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A QUIC implementation SHOULD use information provided by the application to determine how to allocate resources to active streams.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Provide the stream operations described here
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A QUIC implementation MUST provide an interface that includes the operations described in this section.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow protocol-specific implementations to expose only needed operations
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An implementation designed for use with a specific application protocol MAY provide only those operations that are used by that protocol.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow writing data after reserving flow control credit
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An application protocol MAY write data only after stream flow control credit has been successfully reserved to send the written data.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow clean stream termination
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An application protocol MAY end a stream, resulting in a STREAM frame with the FIN bit set.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow abrupt stream termination
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An application protocol MAY reset a stream if the stream is not already in a terminal state, resulting in a RESET_STREAM frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow reading data
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An application protocol MAY read data from a stream.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow aborting stream reads
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An application protocol MAY abort reading a stream and request closure, possibly resulting in a STOP_SENDING frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow stream state-change notifications
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An application protocol MAY request to be informed of stream state changes, including when the peer has opened or reset a stream, when a peer aborts reading on a stream, when new data is available, and when data can or cannot be written to the stream due to flow control.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Choose the correct state machine for unidirectional streams
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Unidirectional streams MUST use either the sending or receiving state machine, depending on the stream type and endpoint role.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use both state machines for bidirectional streams
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Bidirectional streams MUST use both state machines at both endpoints.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow alternate stream state machines with consistent behavior
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An implementation MAY define a different stream state machine as long as its behavior is consistent with an implementation that implements these states.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat Ready as a newly created sendable stream
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The Ready state MUST represent a newly created stream that is able to accept data from the application.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Permit buffering in Ready
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An implementation MAY buffer stream data in the Ready state in preparation for sending.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter Send state on first outbound stream frame
