live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Sending the first STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame MUST cause a sending part of a stream to enter the Send state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow deferred stream ID allocation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An implementation MAY defer allocating a stream ID to a stream until it sends the first STREAM frame and enters the Send state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Start peer-initiated bidirectional senders in Ready
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The sending part of a bidirectional stream initiated by a peer MUST start in the Ready state when the receiving part is created.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Transmit and retransmit in Send
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In the Send state, an endpoint MUST transmit and retransmit as necessary stream data in STREAM frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Respect peer flow control while sending
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint in the Send state MUST respect the flow control limits set by its peer and continue to accept and process MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Restrict Data Sent retransmissions
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: From the Data Sent state, the endpoint MUST retransmit stream data only as necessary.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Stop flow control checks in Data Sent
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint in the Data Sent state MUST NOT need to check flow control limits or send STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames for the stream.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow ignoring MAX_STREAM_DATA in Data Sent
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint in the Data Sent state MAY safely ignore any MAX_STREAM_DATA frames it receives from its peer for that stream.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter Data Recvd after all data is acknowledged
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Once all stream data has been successfully acknowledged, the sending part of the stream MUST enter the Data Recvd state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow application abandonment of stream transmission
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: From any state that is Ready, Send, or Data Sent, an application MAY signal that it wishes to abandon transmission of stream data.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send RESET_STREAM when abandoning transmission
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In either case, the endpoint MUST send a RESET_STREAM frame, which causes the stream to enter the Reset Sent state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Permit RESET_STREAM as the first frame
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY send a RESET_STREAM as the first frame that mentions a stream, causing the sending part of that stream to open and then immediately transition to the Reset Sent state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter Reset Recvd after RESET_STREAM is acknowledged
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Once a packet containing a RESET_STREAM has been acknowledged, the sending part of the stream MUST enter the Reset Recvd state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not track unobservable sending-part states
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The receiving part of a stream MUST NOT track states on the sending part that cannot be observed, such as the Ready state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Track data delivery to the application
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The receiving part of a stream MUST track the delivery of data to the application, including data that cannot be observed by the sender.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Start receiving parts in Recv
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The initial state for the receiving part of a stream MUST be Recv.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter Recv when the peer-side sending part opens
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: For a bidirectional stream, the receiving part MUST enter the Recv state when the sending part initiated by the endpoint enters the Ready state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Open bidirectional streams on peer flow-control or stop-sending frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST open a bidirectional stream when a MAX_STREAM_DATA or STOP_SENDING frame is received from the peer for that stream.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Interpret MAX_STREAM_DATA on an unopened stream as peer opening
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Receiving a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for an unopened stream MUST indicate that the remote peer has opened the stream and is providing flow control credit.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Interpret STOP_SENDING on an unopened stream as a peer desire to stop reception
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Receiving a STOP_SENDING frame for an unopened stream MUST indicate that the remote peer no longer wishes to receive data on this stream.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow reordered peer flow-control or stop-sending frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Either frame MAY arrive before a STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame if packets are lost or reordered.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Buffer received stream data for ordered delivery
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Incoming data MUST be buffered for ordered delivery to the application, including any reassembly needed to place it in the correct order.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Advertise more receive credit as data is consumed
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: As data is consumed by the application and buffer space becomes available, the endpoint MUST send MAX_STREAM_DATA frames to allow the peer to send more data.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Recognize final size when FIN arrives
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When a STREAM frame with a FIN bit is received, the final size of the stream MUST be known.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter Size Known after FIN
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The receiving part of the stream MUST then enter the Size Known state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard further stream frames after all data is received
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: After all data has been received, any STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames for the stream MAY be discarded.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter Data Read after delivery to the application
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Once stream data has been delivered, the stream MUST enter the Data Read state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter Reset Recvd on RESET_STREAM in Recv or Size Known
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Receiving a RESET_STREAM frame in the Recv or Size Known state MUST cause the stream to enter the Reset Recvd state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Remain in Data Recvd when RESET_STREAM is suppressed
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the RESET_STREAM is suppressed, the receiving part of the stream MUST remain in Data Recvd.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Enter Reset Read after the application receives reset notification
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Once the application receives the signal indicating that the stream was reset, the receiving part of the stream MUST transition to the Reset Read state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Forbid terminal-state transmit frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A sender MUST NOT send STREAM, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, or RESET_STREAM frames from a terminal state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Forbid post-reset transmission of STREAM frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A sender MUST NOT send a STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame for a stream in the Reset Sent state or any terminal state after sending a RESET_STREAM frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow delayed receipt of state-changing frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A receiver MAY receive STREAM, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, or RESET_STREAM frames in any state due to delayed delivery of packets carrying them.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Limit MAX_STREAM_DATA to Recv
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The receiver MUST only send MAX_STREAM_DATA frames in the Recv state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow STOP_SENDING except after reset reception
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A receiver MAY send a STOP_SENDING frame in any state where it has not received a RESET_STREAM frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow delayed receipt of receiver-side frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A sender MAY receive MAX_STREAM_DATA or STOP_SENDING frames in any state as a result of delayed delivery of packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Compose bidirectional streams from send and receive parts
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A bidirectional stream MUST be composed of sending and receiving parts.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow composite stream-state representations
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Implementations MAY represent bidirectional stream states as composites of sending and receiving stream states.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Require acknowledgment before closed-state transitions in the example mapping
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Any mapping to a closed or half-closed state MUST require data to be acknowledged before the transition.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow aborting stream reads with an application error code
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If an application is no longer interested in the data it is receiving on a stream, it MAY abort reading the stream and specify an application error code.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Signal aborting reads with STOP_SENDING
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the stream is in the Recv or Size Known state, the transport SHOULD signal aborting reading by sending a STOP_SENDING frame to prompt closure of the stream in the opposite direction.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Count data after STOP_SENDING toward flow control
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: STREAM frames received after sending a STOP_SENDING frame MUST still be counted toward connection and stream flow control even if they are discarded upon receipt.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat STOP_SENDING as a request for RESET_STREAM
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A STOP_SENDING frame MUST request that the receiving endpoint send a RESET_STREAM frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send RESET_STREAM after receiving STOP_SENDING in Ready or Send
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that receives a STOP_SENDING frame MUST send a RESET_STREAM frame if the stream is in the Ready or Send state.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Permit deferred RESET_STREAM in Data Sent
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the stream is in the Data Sent state, the endpoint MAY defer sending the RESET_STREAM frame until the packets containing outstanding data are acknowledged or declared lost.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Prefer RESET_STREAM over retransmission after loss
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If any outstanding data is declared lost, the endpoint SHOULD send a RESET_STREAM frame instead of retransmitting the data.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Copy STOP_SENDING error codes when sending RESET_STREAM
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint SHOULD copy the error code from the STOP_SENDING frame to the RESET_STREAM frame it sends.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow ignoring later RESET_STREAM error codes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that sends a STOP_SENDING frame MAY ignore the error code in any RESET_STREAM frames subsequently received for that stream.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Repeat STOP_SENDING after loss
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint SHOULD send another STOP_SENDING frame if a packet containing a previous STOP_SENDING is lost.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow RESET_STREAM to terminate one direction of a bidirectional stream
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY terminate one direction of a bidirectional stream by sending a RESET_STREAM frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow STOP_SENDING to encourage prompt opposite-direction termination
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY encourage prompt termination in the opposite direction by sending a STOP_SENDING frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Flow-control streams and the whole connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Streams MUST be flow controlled both individually and across a connection as a whole.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Limit bytes on streams and across the connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A QUIC receiver MUST control the maximum amount of data the sender can send on a stream and across all streams at any time.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use limit-based flow control
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: QUIC MUST employ a limit-based flow control scheme in which a receiver advertises the total bytes it is prepared to receive on a given stream or for the entire connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Limit per-stream receive buffer use
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Stream flow control MUST prevent a single stream from consuming the entire receive buffer for a connection by limiting the amount of data that can be sent on each stream.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Advertise larger flow-control limits with MAX frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Subsequently, a receiver MUST send MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frames to advertise larger limits.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Advertise larger connection limits with MAX_DATA
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A receiver MAY advertise a larger limit for a connection by sending a MAX_DATA frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Ignore smaller advertised limits
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Once a receiver advertises a limit for the connection or a stream, advertising a smaller limit MUST have no effect rather than be treated as an error.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow repeated or early credit advertisements
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A receiver MAY send a MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frame multiple times within a round trip or send it early enough to allow time for loss of the frame and subsequent recovery.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow autotuning of flow-control credit
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A receiver MAY use an autotuning mechanism to tune the frequency and amount of advertised additional credit based on a round-trip time estimate and the rate at which the receiving application consumes data.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send flow-control frames opportunistically
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY send frames related to flow control only when there are other frames to send, ensuring that flow control does not cause extra packets to be sent.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not require blocked senders to signal blocking
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A blocked sender MUST NOT be required to send STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Tear down state and ignore later data after RESET_STREAM
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: On receipt of a RESET_STREAM frame, an endpoint MUST tear down state for the matching stream and ignore further data arriving on that stream.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Terminate only one direction on RESET_STREAM
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: RESET_STREAM MUST terminate one direction of a stream abruptly.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Communicate final size reliably
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A sender MUST always communicate the final size of a stream to the receiver reliably, no matter how the stream is terminated.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use STREAM FIN to carry final size
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The final size of a stream MUST be the sum of the Offset and Length fields of a STREAM frame with a FIN flag, including any implicit values.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use RESET_STREAM Final Size to carry final size
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The Final Size field of a RESET_STREAM frame MUST carry the final size value.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat final-size changes as errors
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If a RESET_STREAM or STREAM frame is received indicating a change in the final size for the stream, an endpoint SHOULD respond with an error of type FINAL_SIZE_ERROR.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat data beyond final size as an error
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A receiver SHOULD treat receipt of data at or beyond the final size as an error of type FINAL_SIZE_ERROR, even after a stream is closed.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Limit the cumulative number of incoming streams
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST limit the cumulative number of incoming streams its peer can open.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Restrict stream IDs to the advertised limit
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Only streams with stream IDs less than max_streams * 4 + first_stream_id_of_type MAY be opened.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Set initial stream limits in transport parameters
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Initial limits MUST be set in the transport parameters.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Advertise later stream limits with MAX_STREAMS
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Subsequent limits MUST be advertised using MAX_STREAMS frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Apply separate limits by stream direction
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Separate limits MUST apply to unidirectional and bidirectional streams.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Close on oversized stream-count values in transport parameters
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If an oversized max_streams value is received in a transport parameter, the connection MUST be closed immediately with TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Close on oversized stream-count values in frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If an oversized max_streams value is received in a frame, the connection MUST be closed immediately with FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Ignore smaller advertised stream limits
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Once a receiver advertises a stream limit using the MAX_STREAMS frame, advertising a smaller limit MUST have no effect.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Ignore non-increasing MAX_STREAMS frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: MAX_STREAMS frames that do not increase the stream limit MUST be ignored.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat a QUIC connection as shared client-server state
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A QUIC connection MUST be shared state between a client and a server.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Start every connection with a handshake phase
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Each connection MUST start with a handshake phase during which the two endpoints establish a shared secret using the cryptographic handshake protocol and negotiate the application protocol.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use the handshake to confirm willingness and establish parameters
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The handshake MUST confirm that both endpoints are willing to communicate and establish parameters for the connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow limited connection use during the handshake
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An application protocol MAY use the connection during the handshake phase with some limitations.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow 0-RTT client data before server response
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: 0-RTT MUST allow application data to be sent by a client before receiving a response from the server.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not provide replay protection for 0-RTT
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: 0-RTT MUST NOT provide protection against replay attacks.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow server data before final handshake messages
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A server MAY send application data to a client before it receives the final cryptographic handshake messages that allow it to confirm the identity and liveness of the client.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use connection IDs to enable migration
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Connection IDs MUST allow connections to migrate to a new network path, both as a direct choice of an endpoint and when forced by a change in a middlebox.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Assign each connection a set of CIDs
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Each connection MUST possess a set of connection IDs, each of which can identify the connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Let endpoints choose peer-used connection IDs
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Connection IDs MUST be independently selected by endpoints, with each endpoint selecting the connection IDs that its peer uses.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use CIDs to survive address changes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Connection IDs MUST ensure that changes in lower-layer addressing do not cause packets for a QUIC connection to be delivered to the wrong endpoint.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Make CID selection routable and recognizable
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Each endpoint MUST select connection IDs using an implementation-specific method that allows packets with that connection ID to be routed back to the endpoint and to be identified by the endpoint upon receipt.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use multiple CIDs for privacy
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints MUST use multiple connection IDs so that they can send packets that an observer cannot identify as belonging to the same connection without cooperation from an endpoint.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Include CID fields in long headers
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets with long headers MUST include Source Connection ID and Destination Connection ID fields.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Include only the destination CID in short headers
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets with short headers MUST include only the Destination Connection ID and omit the explicit length.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Know the short-header destination CID length
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The length of the Destination Connection ID field MUST be known to endpoints.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow load balancers to agree on CID handling
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints using a load balancer that routes based on connection ID MAY agree with the load balancer on a fixed length for connection IDs or on an encoding scheme.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Echo client CIDs in Version Negotiation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST echo the connection IDs selected by the client.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Avoid concurrent zero-length-CID connections on the same address tuple
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT use the same IP address and port for multiple concurrent connections with zero-length connection IDs unless it is certain that peer connection migration, NAT rebinding, and client port reuse are not in use.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Associate each CID with a sequence number
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Each connection ID MUST have an associated sequence number to assist in detecting when NEW_CONNECTION_ID or RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames refer to the same value.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use NEW_CONNECTION_ID for additional CIDs
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Additional connection IDs MUST be communicated to the peer using NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not sequence the first client-selected CID or Retry-provided CID
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The connection ID that a client selects for the first Destination Connection ID field it sends and any connection ID provided by a Retry packet MUST NOT be assigned sequence numbers.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Accept packets carrying an issued CID for the connection lifetime
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When an endpoint issues a connection ID, it MUST accept packets that carry this connection ID for the duration of the connection or until its peer invalidates the connection ID via a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat active CIDs as valid at any time
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Connection IDs that are issued and not retired MUST be considered active and valid for use with the current connection at any time in any packet type.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not exceed the peer's active CID limit
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT provide more connection IDs than the peer's limit.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow temporary CID excess only with immediate retirement requirements
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY send connection IDs that temporarily exceed a peer's limit if the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame also requires the retirement of any excess by including a sufficiently large value in the Retire Prior To field.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Close on too many active CIDs
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: After processing a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame and adding and retiring active connection IDs, if the number of active connection IDs exceeds the value advertised in the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter, an endpoint MUST close the connection with an error of type CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow limiting the total number of issued CIDs
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY limit the total number of connection IDs issued for each connection to avoid the risk of running out of connection IDs.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow limiting CID issuance to reduce per-path state
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY also limit the issuance of connection IDs to reduce the amount of per-path state it maintains.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Keep enough peer-usable CIDs for migration
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that initiates migration and requires non-zero-length connection IDs SHOULD ensure that the pool of connection IDs available to its peer allows the peer to use a new connection ID on migration.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Consume CIDs in response to migration
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY consume connection IDs in response to a migrating peer.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Maintain a set of peer-issued CIDs
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST maintain a set of connection IDs received from its peer for use when sending packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Retire a CID by sending RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When the endpoint wishes to remove a connection ID from use, it MUST send a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame to its peer.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Make RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID a no-reuse request
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Sending a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame MUST indicate that the connection ID will not be used again and request that the peer replace it with a new connection ID using a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Prompt peer retirement with an increased Retire Prior To
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY cause its peer to retire connection IDs by sending a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame with an increased Retire Prior To field.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Continue accepting retired CIDs until the peer retires them
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The endpoint SHOULD continue to accept the previously issued connection IDs until they are retired by the peer.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Track at least twice the active CID limit
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint SHOULD allow for sending and tracking a number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames of at least twice the value of the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow treating excessive unretired CIDs as an error
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY treat having connection IDs in need of retirement that exceed this limit as a connection error of type CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Classify incoming packets on receipt
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Incoming packets MUST be classified on receipt.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow existing-connection association or new server connections
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets MAY either be associated with an existing connection or, for servers, potentially create a new connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Try to associate packets with an existing connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints MUST try to associate a packet with an existing connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Process packets that match the existing CID
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the packet has a non-zero-length Destination Connection ID corresponding to an existing connection, QUIC MUST process that packet accordingly.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow fragile zero-length-CID matching strategies
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY use just the destination IP and port or both source and destination addresses for identification.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow Stateless Reset for unattributed packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints MAY send a Stateless Reset for any packets that cannot be attributed to an existing connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard packets inconsistent with connection state
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets that are matched to an existing connection MUST be discarded if the packets are inconsistent with the state of that connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard packets with a different protocol version
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets MUST be discarded if they indicate a different protocol version than that of the connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard packets if packet protection cannot be removed
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets MUST be discarded if removal of packet protection is unsuccessful once the expected keys are available.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Generate a connection error on pre-error processing
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST generate a connection error if it processes the contents of these packets before discovering an error.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Revert changes made while processing weakly protected invalid packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST fully revert any changes made during that processing.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Match client packets by client-selected CID
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Valid packets sent to clients MUST always include a Destination Connection ID that matches a value the client selects.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard packets that do not match an existing client connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets that do not match an existing connection based on Destination Connection ID or, if that value is zero length, local IP address and port MUST be discarded.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow clients to drop or buffer not-yet-decryptable packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client MAY drop packets encrypted with a key it has not yet computed or buffer them in anticipation of later packets that allow it to compute the key.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send Version Negotiation for large unsupported packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If a server receives a packet that indicates an unsupported version and the packet is large enough to initiate a new connection for any supported version, the server SHOULD send a Version Negotiation packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Prefer Version Negotiation when possible
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Servers SHOULD respond with a Version Negotiation packet, provided that the datagram is sufficiently long.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Match supported-version packets by connection ID or address tuple
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets with a supported version or no Version field MUST be matched to a connection using the connection ID or, for packets with zero-length connection IDs, the local address and port.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Ignore premature Handshake packets from clients
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Servers SHOULD ignore any Handshake packets sent before the client receives a server response.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow out-of-band forwarding for simple load balancers
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Servers MAY use an out-of-band mechanism to forward packets to the correct server based on connection ID.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow preferred-address migration for dedicated server addresses
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If servers can use a dedicated server IP address or port other than the one that the client initially connects to, they MAY use the preferred_address transport parameter to request that clients move connections to that dedicated address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow clients to decline preferred addresses
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Clients MAY choose not to use the preferred address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Avoid stateless reset oracles in simple load balancing
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Server deployments that use this simple form of load balancing MUST avoid the creation of a stateless reset oracle.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow clients to open connections
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When implementing the client role, an application protocol MAY open a connection, which begins the exchange described in Section 7.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow clients to enable Early Data
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When implementing the client role, an application protocol MAY enable Early Data when available.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow clients to learn Early Data acceptance
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When implementing the client role, an application protocol MAY be informed when Early Data has been accepted or rejected by a server.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow servers to listen for connections
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When implementing the server role, an application protocol MAY listen for incoming connections, which prepares for the exchange described in Section 7.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow servers to embed application data in resumption tickets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If Early Data is supported, an application protocol MAY embed application-controlled data in the TLS resumption ticket sent to the client.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow servers to use resumption-ticket data for Early Data decisions
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If Early Data is supported, an application protocol MAY retrieve application-controlled data from the client's resumption ticket and accept or reject Early Data based on that information.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow configuring initial stream counts
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In either role, an application protocol MAY configure minimum values for the initial number of permitted streams of each type as communicated in the transport parameters.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow receive-buffer control via flow control limits
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In either role, an application protocol MAY control resource allocation for receive buffers by setting flow control limits both for streams and for the connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow handshake status queries
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In either role, an application protocol MAY identify whether the handshake has completed successfully or is still ongoing.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow connection liveness maintenance
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In either role, an application protocol MAY keep a connection from silently closing by either generating PING frames or requesting that the transport send additional frames before the idle timeout expires.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow immediate connection close
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In either role, an application protocol MAY immediately close the connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Clients that support multiple QUIC versions SHOULD ensure that the first UDP datagram they send is sized to the largest of the minimum datagram sizes from all versions they support, using PADDING frames (Section 19
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Clients that support multiple QUIC versions SHOULD ensure that the first UDP datagram they send is sized to the largest of the minimum datagram sizes from all versions they support, using PADDING frames (Section 19.1) as necessary.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send Version Negotiation with accepted versions
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the version selected by the client is not acceptable to the server, the server MUST respond with a Version Negotiation packet that includes a list of versions the server will accept.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Reject unsupported Version Negotiation attempts
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client that supports only this version of QUIC MUST abandon the current connection attempt if it receives a Version Negotiation packet unless it has received and successfully processed any other packet or the Version Negotiation packet lists the QUIC version selected by the client.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: That supports only this version of QUIC MUST abandon the current connection attempt if it receives a Version Negotiation packet, with the following two exceptions
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client that supports only this version of QUIC MUST abandon the current connection attempt if it receives a Version Negotiation packet, with the following two exceptions.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use reserved versions to test ignoring
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints MAY add reserved versions to any field where unknown or unsupported versions are ignored to test that a peer correctly ignores the value.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use reserved versions to test discarding
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints MAY send packets with a reserved version to test that a peer correctly discards the packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Provide the following properties:
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST provide the following properties:

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Provide authenticated key exchange
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST provide authenticated key exchange.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Always authenticate the server
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST always authenticate the server.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow optional client authentication
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The cryptographic handshake MAY optionally authenticate the client.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Produce distinct keys per connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Every connection MUST produce distinct and unrelated keys.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use handshake keys for 0-RTT and 1-RTT protection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Keying material from the cryptographic handshake MUST be usable for packet protection for both 0-RTT and 1-RTT packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Authenticate transport parameter exchange
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST provide authenticated exchange of transport parameter values for both endpoints.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Protect server transport parameters
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST provide confidentiality protection for server transport parameters.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Authenticate application protocol negotiation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST provide authenticated negotiation of an application protocol.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use Source Connection ID to select the peer-facing Destination Connection ID
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Each endpoint MUST use the Source Connection ID field to specify the connection ID that is used in the Destination Connection ID field of packets being sent to it.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use an unpredictable client Destination Connection ID
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When a client sends its first Initial packet without having previously received an Initial or Retry packet from the server, it MUST populate the Destination Connection ID field with an unpredictable value.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Populate the client Source Connection ID
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The client MUST populate the Source Connection ID field with a value of its choosing and set the Source Connection ID Length field to indicate the length.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Change the Destination Connection ID it uses for sending packets in response to only the first received Initial or Retry packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client MUST change the Destination Connection ID it uses for sending packets in response to only the first received Initial or Retry packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow further Destination Connection ID changes only from NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY make further changes to the Destination Connection ID only if the values are taken from NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard subsequent Initial packets with a different Source Connection ID
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Subsequent Initial packets that include a different Source Connection ID MUST be discarded.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Authenticate connection ID choices through transport parameters
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The choice each endpoint makes about connection IDs during the handshake MUST be authenticated by including all values in transport parameters.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Echo the client Initial Destination Connection ID in original_destination_connection_id
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A server MUST include the Destination Connection ID field from the first Initial packet it received from the client in the original_destination_connection_id transport parameter.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Echo the Retry Source Connection ID when Retry is used
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If it sends a Retry packet, a server MUST also include the Source Connection ID field from the Retry packet in the retry_source_connection_id transport parameter.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The values provided by a peer for these transport parameters MUST match the values that an endpoint used in the Destination and Source Connection ID fields of Initial packets that it sent (and received, for servers)
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The values provided by a peer for these transport parameters MUST match the values that an endpoint used in the Destination and Source Connection ID fields of Initial packets that it sent (and received, for servers).

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat the absence of the initial_source_connection_id transport parameter from either endpoint or the absence of the original_destination_connection_id transport parameter from the server as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST treat the absence of the initial_source_connection_id transport parameter from either endpoint or the absence of the original_destination_connection_id transport parameter from the server as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Treat the following as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR or PROTOCOL_VIOLATION:
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST treat the following as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR or PROTOCOL_VIOLATION:

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The definition of a new transport parameter (Section 7
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The definition of a new transport parameter (Section 7.4.2) MUST specify whether storing the transport parameter for 0-RTT is mandatory, optional, or prohibited.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use remembered values for the following parameters: ack_delay_exponent, max_ack_delay, initial_source_connection_id, original_destination_connection_id, preferred_address, retry_source_connection_id, and stateless_reset_token
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client MUST NOT use remembered values for the following parameters: ack_delay_exponent, max_ack_delay, initial_source_connection_id, original_destination_connection_id, preferred_address, retry_source_connection_id, and stateless_reset_token.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: If 0-RTT data is accepted by the server, the server MUST NOT reduce any limits or alter any values that might be violated by the client with its 0-RTT data
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If 0-RTT data is accepted by the server, the server MUST NOT reduce any limits or alter any values that might be violated by the client with its 0-RTT data.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: In particular, a server that accepts 0-RTT data MUST NOT set values for the following parameters (Section 18
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In particular, a server that accepts 0-RTT data MUST NOT set values for the following parameters (Section 18.2) that are smaller than the remembered values of the parameters.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not use updated transport-parameter values in 0-RTT
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When sending frames in 0-RTT packets, a client MUST NOT use updated values it learns from the server's updated transport parameters or from frames received in 1-RTT packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow 0-RTT only with remembered transport parameters
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Updated values of transport parameters from the handshake MUST apply only to 1-RTT packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Choose to allow more data to be buffered during the handshake
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints MAY choose to allow more data to be buffered during the handshake.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Once the handshake completes, if an endpoint is unable to buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame, it MAY discard that CRYPTO frame and all CRYPTO frames received in the future, or it MAY close the connection with a CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Once the handshake completes, if an endpoint is unable to buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame, it MAY discard that CRYPTO frame and all future CRYPTO frames or close the connection with a CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Containing discarded CRYPTO frames MUST be acknowledged because the packet has been received and processed by the transport even though the CRYPTO frame was discarded
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets containing discarded CRYPTO frames MUST be acknowledged because the packet has been received and processed by the transport even though the CRYPTO frame was discarded.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Limit sending to unvalidated addresses
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: After receiving packets from an address that is not yet validated, an endpoint MUST limit the amount of data it sends to the unvalidated address to three times the amount of data received from that address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Additionally, an endpoint MAY consider the peer address validated if the peer uses a connection ID chosen by the endpoint and the connection ID contains at least 64 bits of entropy
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Additionally, an endpoint MAY consider the peer address validated if the peer uses a connection ID chosen by the endpoint and the connection ID contains at least 64 bits of entropy.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Prior to validating the client address, servers MUST NOT send more than three times as many bytes as the number of bytes they have received
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Prior to validating the client address, servers MUST NOT send more than three times as many bytes as the number of bytes they have received.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: For the purposes of avoiding amplification prior to address validation, servers MUST count all of the payload bytes received in datagrams that are uniquely attributed to a single connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: For the purposes of avoiding amplification prior to address validation, servers MUST count all of the payload bytes received in datagrams that are uniquely attributed to a single connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: To prevent this deadlock, clients MUST send a packet on a Probe Timeout (PTO)
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To prevent this deadlock, clients MUST send a packet on a Probe Timeout (PTO); see Section 6.2 of [QUIC-RECOVERY].

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Specifically, the client MUST send an Initial packet in a UDP datagram that contains at least 1200 bytes if it does not have Handshake keys, and otherwise send a Handshake packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Specifically, the client MUST send an Initial packet in a UDP datagram that contains at least 1200 bytes if it does not have Handshake keys, and otherwise send a Handshake packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Probe on PTO to avoid handshake deadlock
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To prevent deadlock, clients MUST send a packet on a Probe Timeout (PTO).

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: This token MUST be repeated by the client in all Initial packets it sends for that connection after it receives the Retry packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: This token MUST be repeated by the client in all Initial packets it sends for that connection after it receives the Retry packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Instead, the server SHOULD immediately close (Section 10
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Instead, the server SHOULD immediately close (Section 10.2) the connection with an INVALID_TOKEN error.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Validate Retry token returns
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The Retry token MUST be repeated by the client in all Initial packets it sends for that connection after it receives the Retry packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Close on invalid Retry tokens
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If a server receives a client Initial that contains an invalid Retry token but is otherwise valid, it SHOULD immediately close the connection with an INVALID_TOKEN error.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Provide clients with an address validation token during one connection that can be used on a subsequent connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A server MAY provide clients with an address validation token during one connection that can be used on a subsequent connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Include the token in all Initial packets it sends, unless a Retry replaces the token with a newer one
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The client MUST include the token in all Initial packets it sends, unless a Retry replaces the token with a newer one.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Thus, a token SHOULD have an expiration time, which could be either an explicit expiration time or an issued timestamp that can be used to dynamically calculate the expiration time
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Thus, a token SHOULD have an expiration time, which could be either an explicit expiration time or an issued timestamp that can be used to dynamically calculate the expiration time.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Issued with NEW_TOKEN MUST NOT include information that would allow values to be linked by an observer to the connection on which it was issued
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A token issued with NEW_TOKEN MUST NOT include information that would allow values to be linked by an observer to the connection on which it was issued.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Ensure that every NEW_TOKEN frame it sends is unique across all clients, with the exception of those sent to repair losses of previously sent NEW_TOKEN frames
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A server MUST ensure that every NEW_TOKEN frame it sends is unique across all clients, with the exception of those sent to repair losses of previously sent NEW_TOKEN frames.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Information that allows the server to distinguish between tokens from Retry and NEW_TOKEN MAY be accessible to entities other than the server
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Information that allows the server to distinguish between tokens from Retry and NEW_TOKEN MAY be accessible to entities other than the server.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Include a token that is not applicable to the server that it is connecting to, unless the client has the knowledge that the server that issued the token and the server the client is connecting to are jointly managing the tokens
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client MUST NOT include a token that is not applicable to the server that it is connecting to, unless the client has the knowledge that the server that issued the token and the server the client is connecting to are jointly managing the tokens.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: In comparison, a token obtained in a Retry packet MUST be used immediately during the connection attempt and cannot be used in subsequent connection attempts
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: In comparison, a token obtained in a Retry packet MUST be used immediately during the connection attempt and cannot be used in subsequent connection attempts.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Reuse a token from a NEW_TOKEN frame for different connection attempts
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client SHOULD NOT reuse a token from a NEW_TOKEN frame for different connection attempts.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: When a server receives an Initial packet with an address validation token, it MUST attempt to validate the token, unless it has already completed address validation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When a server receives an Initial packet with an address validation token, it MUST attempt to validate the token, unless it has already completed address validation.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: If the token is invalid, then the server SHOULD proceed as if the client did not have a validated address, including potentially sending a Retry packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the token is invalid, then the server SHOULD proceed as if the client did not have a validated address, including potentially sending a Retry packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Clients MAY use tokens obtained on one connection for any connection attempt using the same version
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Clients MAY use tokens obtained on one connection for any connection attempt using the same version.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: For this design to work, the token MUST be covered by integrity protection against modification or falsification by clients
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: For this design to work, the token MUST be covered by integrity protection against modification or falsification by clients.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: If the client IP address has changed, the server MUST adhere to the anti-amplification limit
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the client IP address has changed, the server MUST adhere to the anti-amplification limit; see Section 8.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: To protect against such attacks, servers MUST ensure that replay of tokens is prevented or limited
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To protect against such attacks, servers MUST ensure that replay of tokens is prevented or limited.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Servers SHOULD ensure that tokens sent in Retry packets are only accepted for a short time, as they are returned immediately by clients
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Servers SHOULD ensure that tokens sent in Retry packets are only accepted for a short time, as they are returned immediately by clients.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Tokens that are provided in NEW_TOKEN frames (Section 19
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Tokens that are provided in NEW_TOKEN frames (Section 19.7) need to be valid for longer but SHOULD NOT be accepted multiple times.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Servers are encouraged to allow tokens to be used only once, if possible
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Servers are encouraged to allow tokens to be used only once, if possible; tokens MAY include additional information about clients to further narrow applicability or reuse.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Make address-validation tokens hard to guess and integrity protected
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An address validation token MUST be difficult to guess and, for token-based schemes, covered by integrity protection against modification or falsification by clients.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Protect against token replay
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To protect against replay attacks, servers MUST ensure that replay of tokens is prevented or limited.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames to guard against packet loss
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames to guard against packet loss.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: However, an endpoint SHOULD NOT send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in a single packet
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: However, an endpoint SHOULD NOT send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in a single packet.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use unpredictable data in every PATH_CHALLENGE frame so that it can associate the peer's response with the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The endpoint MUST use unpredictable data in every PATH_CHALLENGE frame so that it can associate the peer's response with the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Expand datagrams that contain a PATH_CHALLENGE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes, unless the anti-amplification limit for the path does not permit sending a datagram of this size
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST expand datagrams that contain a PATH_CHALLENGE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes, unless the anti-amplification limit for the path does not permit sending a datagram of this size.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: To ensure that the path MTU is large enough, the endpoint MUST perform a second path validation by sending a PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a datagram of at least 1200 bytes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To ensure that the path MTU is large enough, the endpoint MUST perform a second path validation by sending a PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a datagram of at least 1200 bytes.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Unlike other cases where datagrams are expanded, endpoints MUST NOT discard datagrams that appear to be too small when they contain PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Unlike other cases where datagrams are expanded, endpoints MUST NOT discard datagrams that appear to be too small when they contain PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use PATH_CHALLENGE to validate a path
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To initiate path validation, an endpoint MUST send a PATH_CHALLENGE frame containing an unpredictable payload on the path to be validated.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: On receiving a PATH_CHALLENGE frame, an endpoint MUST respond by echoing the data contained in the PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a PATH_RESPONSE frame
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: On receiving a PATH_CHALLENGE frame, an endpoint MUST respond by echoing the data contained in the PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a PATH_RESPONSE frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Delay transmission of a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame unless constrained by congestion control
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT delay transmission of a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame unless constrained by congestion control.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: This requirement MUST NOT be enforced by the endpoint that initiates path validation, as that would enable an attack on migration
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: This requirement MUST NOT be enforced by the endpoint that initiates path validation, as that would enable an attack on migration; see Section 9.3.3.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Expand datagrams that contain a PATH_RESPONSE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST expand datagrams that contain a PATH_RESPONSE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: However, an endpoint MUST NOT expand the datagram containing the PATH_RESPONSE if the resulting data exceeds the anti-amplification limit
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: However, an endpoint MUST NOT expand the datagram containing the PATH_RESPONSE if the resulting data exceeds the anti-amplification limit.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Send more than one PATH_RESPONSE frame in response to one PATH_CHALLENGE frame
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send more than one PATH_RESPONSE frame in response to one PATH_CHALLENGE frame; see Section 13.3.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: However, the endpoint MUST initiate another path validation with an expanded datagram to verify that the path supports the required MTU
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: However, the endpoint MUST initiate another path validation with an expanded datagram to verify that the path supports the required MTU.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: That has no valid network path to its peer MAY signal this using the NO_VIABLE_PATH connection error, noting that this is only possible if the network path exists but does not support the required MTU (Section 14)
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that has no valid network path to its peer MAY signal this using the NO_VIABLE_PATH connection error, noting that this is only possible if the network path exists but does not support the required MTU (Section 14).

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Signal no viable path when appropriate
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint that has no valid network path to its peer MAY signal this using the NO_VIABLE_PATH connection error.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: If the peer sent the disable_active_migration transport parameter, an endpoint also MUST NOT send packets (including probing packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the peer sent the disable_active_migration transport parameter, an endpoint also MUST NOT send packets (including probing packets; see Section 9.1) from a different local address to the address the peer used during the handshake, unless the endpoint has acted on a preferred_address transport parameter from the peer.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Forbid migration before handshake confirmation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT initiate connection migration before the handshake is confirmed.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Respect Disable Active Migration
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the peer sent the disable_active_migration transport parameter, an endpoint MUST NOT send packets from a different local address to the address the peer used during the handshake unless the endpoint has acted on a preferred_address transport parameter from the peer.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Validate Peer Address Changes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST perform path validation if it detects any change to a peer's address unless it has previously validated that address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard Packets from Unknown Server Addresses
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If a client receives packets from an unknown server address, the client MUST discard those packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Probe for peer reachability from a new local address using path validation (Section 8
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY probe for peer reachability from a new local address using path validation (Section 8.2) prior to migrating the connection to the new local address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Probe New Local Addresses Before Migration
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY probe for peer reachability from a new local address using path validation before migrating the connection to the new local address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Reset Congestion State on Migration
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When migrating, an endpoint MUST immediately reset its congestion controller and round-trip time estimator for the new path to initial values unless the only change in the peer's address is its port number.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Retain State for Port-Only Changes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When the only change in the peer's address is its port number, an endpoint MAY retain its congestion control state and round-trip estimate instead of reverting to initial values.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Validate ECN Capability After Migration
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST validate ECN capability as described in Section 13.4 when it migrates to a new path.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: If the recipient permits the migration, it MUST send subsequent packets to the new peer address and MUST initiate path validation (Section 8
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the recipient permits the migration, it MUST send subsequent packets to the new peer address and initiate path validation (Section 8.2) to verify the peer's ownership of the address if validation is not already underway.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow data on an unvalidated peer address
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY send data to an unvalidated peer address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Protect unvalidated peer-address traffic
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST protect against potential attacks as described in Sections 9.3.1 and 9.3.2 when it sends data to an unvalidated peer address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Skip validation of a peer address if that address has been seen recently
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY skip validation of a peer address if that address has been seen recently.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: After verifying a new client address, the server SHOULD send new address validation tokens (Section 8) to the client
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: After verifying a new client address, the server SHOULD send new address validation tokens (Section 8) to the client.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Initiate Path Validation After Permitting Migration
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the recipient permits the migration, it MUST initiate path validation to verify the peer's ownership of the address if validation is not already underway.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Protect Against Address-Spoofing Attacks
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MUST protect against potential attacks as described in Sections 9.3.1 and 9.3.2.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow Abandoning Other Path Validation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY abandon any path validation for other addresses after changing the address to which it sends non-probing packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Limit Sending Until Address Validation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Until a peer's address is deemed valid, an endpoint MUST limit the amount of data it sends to that address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: To protect the connection from failing due to such a spurious migration, an endpoint MUST revert to using the last validated peer address when validation of a new peer address fails
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To protect the connection from failing due to such a spurious migration, an endpoint MUST revert to using the last validated peer address when validation of a new peer address fails.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: For instance, an endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to any further incoming packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: For instance, an endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to any further incoming packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Revert to the Last Validated Peer Address
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When validation of a new peer address fails, an endpoint MUST revert to using the last validated peer address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow Stateless Reset After Silent Close
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: After discarding all connection state, an endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to any further incoming packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use Heuristics for Attack Detection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY use heuristics to improve detection of this style of attack.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Sent on the old path MUST NOT contribute to congestion control or RTT estimation for the new path
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Packets sent on the old path MUST NOT contribute to congestion control or RTT estimation for the new path.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use updated congestion state only after confirming the peer address
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: On confirming a peer's ownership of its new address, an endpoint MUST immediately reset the congestion controller and round-trip time estimator for the new path to initial values unless the only change in the peer's address is its port number.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Retain congestion state for port-only changes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Because port-only changes are commonly the result of NAT rebinding or other middlebox activity, the endpoint MAY instead retain its congestion control state and round-trip estimate in those cases instead of reverting to initial values.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Keep ACK coverage across multiple paths
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A receiver of packets on multiple paths MUST still send ACK frames covering all received packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Retain State for Port-Only Peer Changes
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: When the only change in the peer's address is its port number, an endpoint MAY retain its congestion control state and round-trip estimate instead of reverting to initial values.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow Probe-Packet Loss Exceptions
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A sender MAY make exceptions for probe packets so their loss detection is independent and does not unduly cause the congestion controller to reduce its sending rate.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow a Separate PATH_CHALLENGE Timer
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint MAY set a separate timer when a PATH_CHALLENGE is sent, and the timer is canceled if the corresponding PATH_RESPONSE is received.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow Retrying PATH_CHALLENGE on Timeout
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the timer fires before the PATH_RESPONSE is received, an endpoint MAY send a new PATH_CHALLENGE and restart the timer for a longer period of time.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do Not Make the PATH_CHALLENGE Timer More Aggressive
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: This timer MUST NOT be more aggressive.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: At any time, endpoints MAY change the Destination Connection ID they transmit with to a value that has not been used on another path
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: At any time, endpoints MAY change the Destination Connection ID they transmit with to a value that has not been used on another path.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Prevent connection-id reuse across destination addresses
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Similarly, an endpoint MUST NOT reuse a connection ID when sending to more than one destination address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Due to network changes outside the control of its peer, an endpoint might receive packets from a new source address with the same Destination Connection ID field value, in which case it MAY continue to use the current connection ID with the new remote address while still sending from the same local address
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Due to network changes outside the control of its peer, an endpoint might receive packets from a new source address with the same Destination Connection ID field value, in which case it MAY continue to use the current connection ID with the new remote address while still sending from the same local address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Limit use of the zero-length connection ID for migration
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: An endpoint SHOULD NOT initiate migration with a peer that has requested a zero-length connection ID, because traffic over the new path might be trivially linkable to traffic over the old one.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Keep address changes infrequent
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Changing address can cause a peer to reset its congestion control state, so addresses SHOULD only be changed infrequently.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Provide new connection IDs before peers migrate
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: To ensure that migration is possible and packets sent on different paths cannot be correlated, endpoints SHOULD provide new connection IDs before peers migrate.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Keep Provided Connection IDs Unlinkable
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints MUST ensure that connection IDs they provide cannot be linked by any other entity.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow Reuse with the Same Local Address
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If an endpoint receives packets from a new source address with the same Destination Connection ID field value, it MAY continue to use the current connection ID with the new remote address while still sending from the same local address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: If a client receives packets from a new server address when the client has not initiated a migration to that address, the client SHOULD discard these packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If a client receives packets from a new server address when the client has not initiated a migration to that address, the client SHOULD discard these packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discard Unexpected Server-Address Packets
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If a client receives packets from a new server address when it has not initiated a migration to that address, the client SHOULD discard those packets.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Servers MAY communicate a preferred address of each address family (IPv4 and IPv6) to allow clients to pick the one most suited to their network attachment
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Servers MAY communicate a preferred address of each address family (IPv4 and IPv6) to allow clients to pick the one most suited to their network attachment.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Once the handshake is confirmed, the client SHOULD select one of the two addresses provided by the server and initiate path validation (see Section 8
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Once the handshake is confirmed, the client SHOULD select one of the two addresses provided by the server and initiate path validation (see Section 8.2).

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Begin sending packets to the new server address after successful validation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: As soon as path validation succeeds, the client SHOULD begin sending all future packets to the new server address using the new connection ID.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Discontinue use of the old server address after successful validation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: As soon as path validation succeeds, the client SHOULD discontinue use of the old server address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Keep using the original server address after failed validation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If path validation fails, the client MUST continue sending all future packets to the server's original IP address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Convey a Preferred Address in the TLS Handshake
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A server MUST convey a preferred address by including the preferred_address transport parameter in the TLS handshake.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Allow Per-Family Preferred Addresses
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Servers MAY communicate a preferred address of each address family to allow clients to pick the one most suited to their network attachment.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use an Unused Active Connection ID for Preferred-Address Migration
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client MUST construct packets using any previously unused active connection ID, taken from either the preferred_address transport parameter or a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Move Future Packets to the New Server Address After Validation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: As soon as path validation succeeds, the client SHOULD begin sending all future packets to the new server address using the new connection ID and discontinue use of the old server address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: That migrates to a preferred address MUST validate the address it chooses before migrating
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client that migrates to a preferred address MUST validate the address it chooses before migrating; see Section 21.5.3.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Do not use preferred-address values for other connections
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The addresses that a server provides in the preferred_address transport parameter MUST be treated as valid only for the connection in which they are provided.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use these for other connections, including connections that are resumed from the current connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client MUST NOT use these for other connections, including connections that are resumed from the current connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Respond to PATH_CHALLENGE with PATH_RESPONSE
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If the received packet contains a PATH_CHALLENGE frame, the server MUST send a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame as described in Section 8.2.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Move Exclusively to the Preferred Address After Validation
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Once the server has completed path validation and has received a non-probing packet with a new largest packet number on its preferred address, the server MUST send non-probing packets to the client exclusively from its preferred IP address.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Restrict Preferred-Address Values to the Current Connection
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: A client MUST NOT use the addresses provided in the preferred_address transport parameter for other connections, including connections that are resumed from the current connection.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Servers SHOULD initiate path validation to the client's new address upon receiving a probe packet from a different address
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Servers SHOULD initiate path validation to the client's new address upon receiving a probe packet from a different address; see Section 8.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Keep preferred-address connection IDs path-agnostic
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The connection ID provided in the `preferred_address` transport parameter MAY be used independently of the addresses that are provided.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Use the preferred-address connection ID on any path
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The connection ID is provided to ensure that the client has a connection ID available for migration, but the client MAY use this connection ID on any path.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Protect Preferred-Address Traffic from Attacks
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: If packets received at the server's preferred address have a different source address than was observed from the client during the handshake, the server MUST protect against potential attacks as described in Sections 9.3.1 and 9.3.2.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: That send data using IPv6 SHOULD apply an IPv6 flow label in compliance with [RFC6437], unless the local API does not allow setting IPv6 flow labels
