live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints that send data using IPv6 SHOULD apply an IPv6 flow label in compliance with [RFC6437], unless the local API does not allow setting IPv6 flow labels.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: The flow label generation MUST be designed to minimize the chances of linkability with a previously used flow label, as a stable flow label would enable correlating activity on multiple paths
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The flow label generation MUST be designed to minimize the chances of linkability with a previously used flow label, as a stable flow label would enable correlating activity on multiple paths; see Section 9.5.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Apply IPv6 Flow Labels
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: Endpoints that send data using IPv6 SHOULD apply an IPv6 flow label in compliance with [RFC6437] unless the local API does not allow setting IPv6 flow labels.

live_ids_not_in_staged.title: Minimize Flow-Label Linkability
live_ids_not_in_staged.statement: The flow label generation MUST be designed to minimize the chances of linkability with a previously used flow label.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Authenticate packet contents
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: QUIC MUST authenticate the entirety of each packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Encrypt packet contents
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: QUIC MUST encrypt as much of each packet as is practical.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Streams are ordered byte sequences
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: QUIC streams MUST be ordered sequences of bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Bidirectional streams allow both endpoints to send
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Bidirectional streams MUST allow both endpoints to send data.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Unidirectional streams allow one endpoint to send
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Unidirectional streams MUST allow a single endpoint to send data.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Bound data sent with credit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A credit-based scheme MUST bound the amount of data that can be sent.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit stream creation with credit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A credit-based scheme MUST limit stream creation.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Connections are not bound to one path
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: QUIC connections MUST NOT be strictly bound to a single network path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Migration uses connection identifiers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Connection migration MUST use connection identifiers to allow connections to transfer to a new network path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Client-only migration in version 1
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In this version of QUIC, only clients MAY migrate.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Graceful shutdown
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Applications MAY manage a graceful shutdown.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Immediate teardown on errors
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Errors MAY cause immediate connection teardown.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Stateless termination after state loss
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stateless mechanism MAY provide for termination of connections after one endpoint has lost state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Timeout negotiation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MAY negotiate a timeout period.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: QUIC packet definition
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A QUIC packet MUST be a complete processable unit of QUIC that can be encapsulated in a UDP datagram.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Multiple QUIC packets per datagram
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: One or more QUIC packets MAY be encapsulated in a single UDP datagram.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ack-eliciting packet definition
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A QUIC packet containing frames other than ACK, PADDING, and CONNECTION_CLOSE MUST be an ack-eliciting packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ack-eliciting packets prompt acknowledgments
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An ack-eliciting packet MUST cause a recipient to send an acknowledgment.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Carry data in one direction
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Unidirectional streams MUST carry data in one direction, from the initiator of the stream to its peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Identify streams with numeric IDs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stream MUST be identified within a connection by a numeric value referred to as the stream ID.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Least significant bit identifies stream initiator
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The least significant bit (0x01) of the stream ID MUST identify the initiator of the stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Client-initiated streams use even IDs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Client-initiated streams MUST have even-numbered stream IDs (with the bit set to 0).

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Server-initiated streams use odd IDs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Server-initiated streams MUST have odd-numbered stream IDs (with the bit set to 1).

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Second least significant bit distinguishes stream direction
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The second least significant bit (0x02) of the stream ID MUST distinguish between bidirectional streams and unidirectional streams.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Two low bits identify one of four stream types
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The two least significant bits from a stream ID MUST identify a stream as one of four types.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: 0x00 maps to client-initiated bidirectional streams
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stream ID with bits 0x00 MUST identify a client-initiated, bidirectional stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: 0x01 maps to server-initiated bidirectional streams
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stream ID with bits 0x01 MUST identify a server-initiated, bidirectional stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: 0x02 maps to client-initiated unidirectional streams
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stream ID with bits 0x02 MUST identify a client-initiated, unidirectional stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: 0x03 maps to server-initiated unidirectional streams
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stream ID with bits 0x03 MUST identify a server-initiated, unidirectional stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Stream spaces start at their minimum values
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The stream space for each type MUST begin at the minimum value (0x00 through 0x03, respectively).

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Out-of-order stream IDs open lower-numbered streams
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stream ID that is used out of order MUST result in all streams of that type with lower-numbered stream IDs also being opened.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Buffer out-of-order stream data
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST buffer out-of-order data, up to the advertised flow control limit, to deliver an ordered byte stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Optionally deliver stream data out of order
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Implementations MAY offer the ability to deliver data out of order to a receiving application.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow discarding already received data
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Previously received data MAY be discarded.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Keep duplicate stream data stable
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Data at a given offset MUST NOT change when sent multiple times.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat streams as byte-stream abstractions only
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Streams MUST be treated as ordered byte-stream abstractions with no other structure visible to QUIC.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not preserve STREAM frame boundaries
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: STREAM frame boundaries MUST NOT be preserved when data is transmitted, retransmitted after packet loss, or delivered to the application at a receiver.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Write data after reserving flow control credit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An application protocol MAY write data only after reserving stream flow control credit (Section 4.1) for the data to be sent.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: End stream with FIN
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An application protocol MAY end the stream by sending a STREAM frame (Section 19.8) with the FIN bit set.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reset non-terminal stream
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An application protocol MAY reset the stream by sending a RESET_STREAM frame (Section 19.4) if the stream is not already in a terminal state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Abort stream reading and request closure
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An application protocol MAY abort reading of the stream and request closure, possibly resulting in a STOP_SENDING frame (Section 19.5).

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Request stream state-change notifications
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An application protocol MAY request stream state-change notifications for peer open/reset, peer read abort, new data availability, and flow-control writeability.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use the correct state machine for unidirectional streams
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A unidirectional stream MUST use either the sending or receiving state machine, depending on the stream type and endpoint role.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use both state machines for bidirectional streams
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A bidirectional stream MUST use both state machines at both endpoints.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Opening either side opens bidirectional streams in both directions
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: For a bidirectional stream, opening either the send side or the receive side MUST cause the stream to open in both directions.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Off-path attacker cannot block client migration
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An on-path attacker MUST be unable to prevent a client from migrating to a path for which the attacker is not on-path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Off-path attacker cannot close connection after handshake
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An off-path attacker MUST NOT be able to cause a connection to close after the handshake completes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Data Recvd after all ACKs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When all stream data has been successfully acknowledged, a sending stream in the Data Sent state MUST enter the Data Recvd state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Data Sent on STREAM with FIN
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sending stream in the Send state MUST enter the Data Sent state when the endpoint sends a STREAM frame containing the FIN bit.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Reset Recvd on ACK
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sending stream in the Reset Sent state MUST enter the Reset Recvd state when an ACK is received.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Reset Sent from Data Sent on RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sending stream in the Data Sent state MUST enter the Reset Sent state when the endpoint sends RESET_STREAM.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Reset Sent from Ready on RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sending stream in the Ready state MUST enter the Reset Sent state when the endpoint sends RESET_STREAM.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Reset Sent from Send on RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sending stream in the Send state MUST enter the Reset Sent state when the endpoint sends RESET_STREAM.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Send on STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sending stream in the Ready state MUST enter the Send state when the endpoint sends a STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Application opens initiated sending part
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The application MUST open the sending part of an endpoint-initiated stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ready state accepts application data
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A newly created stream in the Ready state MUST accept application data.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: First STREAM causes Send
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Sending the first STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame on a stream MUST cause the sending part of the stream to enter the Send state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Peer-initiated bidirectional streams start Ready
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The sending part of a peer-initiated bidirectional stream MUST start in the Ready state when the receiving part is created.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send state transmits stream data in STREAM frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In the Send state, an endpoint MUST transmit and retransmit stream data in STREAM frames as necessary.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Process MAX_STREAM_DATA frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint in the Send state MUST continue to accept and process MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Respect peer flow control limits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint in the Send state MUST respect the flow control limits set by its peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retransmit only as needed in Data Sent
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: From the Data Sent state, the endpoint MUST only retransmit stream data as necessary.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Omit STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED in Data Sent
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint in the Data Sent state MAY omit sending STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames for the stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Skip flow control checks in Data Sent
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint in the Data Sent state MAY skip checking flow control limits for the stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ignore MAX_STREAM_DATA in Data Sent
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint in the Data Sent state MAY ignore any MAX_STREAM_DATA frames it receives for the stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Data Recvd after all data is acknowledged
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When all stream data has been successfully acknowledged, the sending part of the stream MUST enter the Data Recvd state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Make Data Recvd terminal
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Data Recvd state MUST be terminal.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send RESET_STREAM after abandonment or STOP_SENDING
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In either case, the endpoint MUST send a RESET_STREAM frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Transition to Reset Sent on RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Sending a RESET_STREAM frame MUST cause the stream to enter the Reset Sent state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow first-frame RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY send a RESET_STREAM as the first frame that mentions a stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Transition to Reset Sent on first-frame RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Sending RESET_STREAM as the first frame that mentions a stream MUST cause the sending part of that stream to open and then immediately transition to the Reset Sent state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Reset Recvd after RESET_STREAM acknowledgment
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once a packet containing RESET_STREAM has been acknowledged, the sending part of the stream MUST enter the Reset Recvd state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Make Reset Recvd terminal
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Reset Recvd state MUST be terminal.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not track unobservable sending states
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The receiving part of a stream MUST not track sending-part states that cannot be observed, such as the Ready state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Create receiving part when bidirectional sending part is created
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The receiving part of a bidirectional stream MUST be created when the sending part is created.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Create receiving part when higher-numbered stream is created
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The receiving part of a stream MUST be created when a higher-numbered stream is created.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Data Read after application reads all data
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The receiving part of a stream in the "Data Recvd" state MUST enter "Data Read" when the application reads all data.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Data Recvd after all data arrives
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The receiving part of a stream in the "Size Known" state MUST enter "Data Recvd" when all data is received.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Reset Read after application reads reset
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The receiving part of a stream in the "Reset Recvd" state MUST enter "Reset Read" when the application reads the reset.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Reset Recvd on RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The receiving part of a stream MUST enter "Reset Recvd" when a RESET_STREAM frame is received.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Size Known on STREAM with FIN
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The receiving part of a stream in the "Recv" state MUST enter "Size Known" when a STREAM frame with FIN is received.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Start receiving part in Recv
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The initial state for the receiving part of a stream MUST be "Recv".

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat MAX_STREAM_DATA on unopened streams as peer-opened
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Receiving a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for an unopened stream MUST indicate that the peer has opened the stream and is providing flow-control credit.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Interpret STOP_SENDING on unopened streams as peer-cancelled
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Receiving a STOP_SENDING frame for an unopened stream MUST indicate that the peer no longer wishes to receive data on the stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Learn final stream size on STREAM FIN
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When a STREAM frame with FIN is received, the final size of the stream MUST be known.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Stop sending MAX_STREAM_DATA in Size Known
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In the Size Known state, the endpoint MUST not send MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard stream frames after all data is received
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An implementation MAY discard STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames for the stream after all data has been received.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Data Read after delivery
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When stream data has been delivered, the stream MUST enter the "Data Read" state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat Data Read as terminal
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The "Data Read" state MUST be terminal.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter Reset Recvd on RESET_STREAM in Recv or Size Known
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Receiving a RESET_STREAM frame in the "Recv" or "Size Known" state MUST cause the stream to enter the "Reset Recvd" state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow delivery after RESET_STREAM reception
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An implementation MAY deliver stream data after a RESET_STREAM is received.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow RESET_STREAM suppression when data is already buffered
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A RESET_STREAM signal MAY be suppressed or withheld if stream data is completely received and is buffered to be read by the application.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Suppressing RESET_STREAM leaves the receiver in Data Recvd
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the RESET_STREAM is suppressed, the receiving part of the stream MUST remain in the "Data Recvd" state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Transition to Reset Read on reset signal
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once the application receives the signal indicating that the stream was reset, the receiving part of the stream MUST transition to the "Reset Read" state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat Reset Read as terminal
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The "Reset Read" state MUST be terminal.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Stream state-affecting frames are limited to three types
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sender MUST use only STREAM, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, and RESET_STREAM frames to affect stream state at either the sender or the receiver.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Terminal stream states forbid state-affecting sender frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sender MUST NOT send any of these frames from a terminal state ("Data Recvd" or "Reset Recvd").

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reset-sent and terminal states forbid STREAM frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sender MUST NOT send a STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame for a stream in the "Reset Sent" state or any terminal state after sending a RESET_STREAM frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: MAX_STREAM_DATA is sent only in Recv
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The receiver MUST send MAX_STREAM_DATA frames only in the "Recv" state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: STOP_SENDING is permitted before reset receipt
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A receiver MAY send a STOP_SENDING frame in any state where it has not received a RESET_STREAM frame, that is, states other than "Reset Recvd" or "Reset Read".

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Require acknowledgment before closed or half-closed transitions
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Data MUST be acknowledged before the transition to a closed or half-closed state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Map closed state from data received and data read
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The composite state MUST be closed when the sending part is Data Recvd and the receiving part is Data Recvd / Data Read.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Map closed state from data received and reset read
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The composite state MUST be closed when the sending part is Data Recvd and the receiving part is Reset Recvd / Reset Read.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Map closed state from reset sent and data read
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The composite state MUST be closed when the sending part is Reset Sent / Reset Recvd and the receiving part is Data Recvd / Data Read.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Map closed state from reset sent and reset read
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The composite state MUST be closed when the sending part is Reset Sent / Reset Recvd and the receiving part is Reset Recvd / Reset Read.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Map half-closed local state from data received
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The composite state MUST be half-closed (local) when the sending part is Data Recvd and the receiving part is Recv / Size Known.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Map half-closed local state from reset sent
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The composite state MUST be half-closed (local) when the sending part is Reset Sent / Reset Recvd and the receiving part is Recv / Size Known.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Map half-closed remote state from data read
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The composite state MUST be half-closed (remote) when the sending part is Ready / Send / Data Sent and the receiving part is Data Recvd / Data Read.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Map half-closed remote state from reset read
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The composite state MUST be half-closed (remote) when the sending part is Ready / Send / Data Sent and the receiving part is Reset Recvd / Reset Read.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Map idle composite state
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The composite state MUST be idle when the sending part is No Stream / Ready and the receiving part is No Stream / Recv.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Map open composite state
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The composite state MUST be open when the sending part is Ready / Send / Data Sent and the receiving part is Recv / Size Known.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Define idle stream state
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stream MUST be considered idle if it has not yet been created or if the receiving part of the stream is in the Recv state without yet having received any frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow aborting reads with an application error
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If an application is no longer interested in stream data, it MAY abort reading the stream and specify an application error code.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Signal STOP_SENDING for Recv or Size Known
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the stream is in the "Recv" or "Size Known" state, the transport SHOULD send STOP_SENDING to prompt closure in the opposite direction.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow discarding STREAM frames after STOP_SENDING
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: STREAM frames received after sending STOP_SENDING MAY be discarded upon receipt.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Count STREAM frames after STOP_SENDING
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: STREAM frames received after sending STOP_SENDING MUST still be counted toward connection and stream flow control.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send RESET_STREAM in Ready or Send after STOP_SENDING
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that receives STOP_SENDING MUST send RESET_STREAM if the stream is in the "Ready" or "Send" state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow deferring RESET_STREAM in Data Sent
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the stream is in the "Data Sent" state, the endpoint MAY defer RESET_STREAM until outstanding data is acknowledged or declared lost.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Prefer RESET_STREAM when outstanding data is lost
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If outstanding data is declared lost, the endpoint SHOULD send RESET_STREAM instead of retransmitting it.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow any application error code in RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY use any application error code in RESET_STREAM.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Copy STOP_SENDING error code to RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD copy the STOP_SENDING error code to RESET_STREAM.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ignore RESET_STREAM error code after STOP_SENDING
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that sends STOP_SENDING MAY ignore the error code in later RESET_STREAM frames for that stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retransmit lost STOP_SENDING frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD send another STOP_SENDING frame if a packet containing a previous STOP_SENDING frame is lost.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Avoid STOP_SENDING after stream completion
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD NOT send a STOP_SENDING frame once either all stream data or a RESET_STREAM frame has been received for the stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Control data across all streams
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A QUIC receiver MUST control the maximum amount of data the sender can send across all streams at any time.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Control data on each stream
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A QUIC receiver MUST control the maximum amount of data the sender can send on a stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Advertise receive limits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A receiver MUST advertise the limit of total bytes it is prepared to receive on a given stream or for the entire connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit stream flow control
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Stream flow control MUST limit the amount of data that can be sent on each stream so a single stream does not consume the entire receive buffer for a connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Advertise larger connection limits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A receiver MAY advertise larger connection limits to a sender by sending MAX_DATA frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Advertise larger stream limits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A receiver MAY advertise larger stream limits to a sender by sending MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Define MAX_DATA aggregate offset
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A MAX_DATA frame MUST indicate the maximum of the sum of the absolute byte offsets of all streams.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Smaller advertised limits are not errors
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Advertising a smaller limit MUST NOT be an error once a receiver has advertised a limit for the connection or a stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Smaller advertised limits have no effect
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Advertising a smaller limit MUST have no effect once a receiver has advertised a limit for the connection or a stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Block at the flow-control limit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If a sender has sent data up to the limit, it MUST be unable to send new data and is considered blocked.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow repeated limit updates
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: To avoid blocking a sender, a receiver MAY send a MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frame multiple times within a round trip or send it early enough to allow time for loss of the frame and subsequent recovery.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow blocked sender to omit flow-control frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A blocked sender MAY omit `STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED` or `DATA_BLOCKED` frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Account stream credit for connection-level flow control
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MUST account for consumed flow control credit on every stream at the connection level until all bytes are accounted for.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ignore data after RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: On receipt of a RESET_STREAM frame, an endpoint MUST ignore further data arriving on that stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Tear down stream state on RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: On receipt of a RESET_STREAM frame, an endpoint MUST tear down state for the matching stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reset one stream direction abruptly
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A RESET_STREAM frame MUST terminate one direction of a stream abruptly.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Final size equals consumed flow-control credit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The final size of a stream MUST be the amount of flow control credit consumed by the stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Communicate final size reliably
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sender MUST communicate the final size of a stream to the receiver reliably, no matter how the stream is terminated.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Define final size from STREAM FIN fields
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A STREAM frame with a FIN flag MUST define the final size as the sum of the Offset and Length fields, which might be implicit.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Carry final size in RESET_STREAM
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Final Size field of a RESET_STREAM frame MUST carry the final size.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Know the final size when the stream state becomes known
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST know the final size for a stream when the receiving part of the stream enters the Size Known or Reset Recvd state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Respond with FINAL_SIZE_ERROR on final-size change
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD respond with a FINAL_SIZE_ERROR if a RESET_STREAM or STREAM frame is received indicating a change in the final size for the stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat data at or beyond final size as FINAL_SIZE_ERROR
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A receiver SHOULD treat receipt of data at or beyond the final size as a FINAL_SIZE_ERROR, even after a stream is closed.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not open streams at or beyond the concurrency limit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT open streams with a stream ID greater than or equal to (max_streams * 4 + first_stream_id_of_type).

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Close on oversized MAX_STREAMS frame
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The connection MUST be closed immediately with a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR if a MAX_STREAMS frame is received with a value greater than 2^60.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Close on oversized max_streams transport parameter
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The connection MUST be closed immediately with a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR if a max_streams transport parameter is received with a value greater than 2^60.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ignore non-increasing MAX_STREAMS frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: MAX_STREAMS frames that do not increase the stream limit MUST be ignored.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow server application data before final handshake messages
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MAY send application data to a client before receiving the final cryptographic handshake messages that confirm the client's identity and liveness.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Authenticated packet integrity
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT accept a packet if any authenticated portion has been modified.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Select connection IDs that support routing and identification
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each endpoint MUST select connection IDs that allow packets to be routed back to the endpoint and identified upon receipt.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include destination connection ID in long headers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets with long headers MUST include a Destination Connection ID field.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include source connection ID in long headers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets with long headers MUST include a Source Connection ID field.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Short headers include only the destination connection ID
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets with short headers (Section 17.3) MUST include only the Destination Connection ID field.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Short headers omit the explicit length
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets with short headers (Section 17.3) MUST omit the explicit length.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Echo client-selected connection IDs in Version Negotiation packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST echo the client's connection IDs.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Forbid concurrent zero-length CID connections on the same address and port
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT use the same IP address and port for multiple concurrent connections with zero-length connection IDs, unless it is certain that those protocol features are not in use.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Associate sequence numbers with connection IDs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each connection ID MUST have an associated sequence number.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: First destination connection ID is unnumbered
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The connection ID that a client selects for the first Destination Connection ID field it sends MUST be unnumbered.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retry-provided connection IDs are unnumbered
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Any connection ID provided by a Retry packet MUST be unnumbered.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Accept packets carrying issued connection IDs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When an endpoint issues a connection ID, it MUST accept packets that carry this connection ID for the duration of the connection or until its peer invalidates the connection ID via a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame (Section 19.16).

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Active connection IDs are valid at any time
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Any active connection ID MUST be valid for use with the current connection at any time, in any packet type.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Issued and unretired connection IDs are active
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Connection IDs that are issued and not retired MUST be considered active.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not exceed peer connection ID limit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST provide no more connection IDs than the peer's limit.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send connection IDs above a peer limit when retirement is required
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY temporarily exceed a peer's limit if the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame requires retirement of the excess by including a sufficiently large Retire Prior To value.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Close when active connection IDs exceed the advertised limit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: After processing a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame, if the number of active connection IDs exceeds the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter, an endpoint MUST close the connection with CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit connection ID issuance to reduce per-path state
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY limit the issuance of connection IDs.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit the total number of connection IDs issued per connection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY limit the total number of connection IDs issued for each connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Keep enough connection IDs available for migration
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that initiates migration and requires non-zero-length connection IDs SHOULD ensure its peer can use a new connection ID on migration.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Maintain peer connection IDs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST maintain a set of connection IDs received from its peer, any of which it can use when sending packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retire connection IDs before removing them from use
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When an endpoint wishes to remove a connection ID from use, it MUST send a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame to its peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Make RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames retire the CID and request replacement
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame MUST indicate that the connection ID will not be used again and request that the peer replace it with a new connection ID using a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use increased Retire Prior To to retire connection IDs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that sends a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame with an increased Retire Prior To field MUST cause its peer to retire the corresponding connection IDs.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Track sufficient RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD allow sending and tracking a number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames of at least twice the value of the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat excess unretired connection IDs as a connection error
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY choose to treat having connection IDs in need of retirement that exceed this limit as a connection error of type CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Process packets for existing connections
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the packet has a non-zero-length Destination Connection ID corresponding to an existing connection, QUIC MUST process the packet as part of that connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send Stateless Reset for unattributable packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MAY send a Stateless Reset for any packet that cannot be attributed to an existing connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard inconsistent packets for matched connections
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets matched to an existing connection MUST be discarded if they are inconsistent with the state of that connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Revert or error on early packet processing
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If an endpoint processes the contents of these packets before discovering an error, it MUST generate a connection error or fully revert any changes made during that processing.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Destination Connection ID matches client selection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Valid packets sent to clients MUST include a Destination Connection ID that matches a value the client selects.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard packets that do not match a connection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets that do not match an existing connection, based on Destination Connection ID or, if this value is zero length, local IP address and port, MUST be discarded.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Drop or buffer packets before key computation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The client MAY drop these packets or buffer them in anticipation of later packets that allow it to compute the key.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send Version Negotiation for unsupported versions
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If a server receives a packet that indicates an unsupported version and the packet is large enough to initiate a new connection for any supported version, the server SHOULD send a Version Negotiation packet as described in Section 6.1.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow different semantics in first unsupported-version packet
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The first packet for an unsupported version MAY use different semantics and encodings for version-specific fields.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Respond with Version Negotiation packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Servers SHOULD respond with a Version Negotiation packet when the datagram is sufficiently long.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Match supported-version packets to connections
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets with a supported version, or no Version field, MUST be matched to a connection using the connection ID or, for packets with zero-length connection IDs, the local address and port.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ignore Handshake packets before a server response
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Servers SHOULD ignore any Handshake packets received prior to receiving a server response.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use preferred_address to request connection migration
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MAY use the preferred_address transport parameter to request that clients move connections to a dedicated server IP address or port other than the one the client initially connects to.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Avoid stateless reset oracle in simple load balancing
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Server deployments that use this simple form of load balancing MUST avoid creating a stateless reset oracle.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send Version Negotiation packets for new-connection attempts
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST send a Version Negotiation packet in response to each packet that might initiate a new connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Omit Version Negotiation on undersized datagrams
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MAY omit sending a Version Negotiation packet if the datagram it receives is smaller than the minimum size specified in a different version.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include accepted versions in Version Negotiation packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST include a list of versions that the server will accept.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Respond with Version Negotiation for unacceptable versions
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the version selected by the client is not acceptable to the server, the server MUST respond with a Version Negotiation packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Authenticate the server
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST authenticate the server.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Optionally authenticate the client
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The cryptographic handshake MAY authenticate the client.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Produce distinct and unrelated keys per connection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each connection MUST produce distinct and unrelated keys.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use keying material for 0-RTT and 1-RTT packet protection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Keying material MUST be usable for packet protection for both 0-RTT and 1-RTT packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Support authenticated application protocol negotiation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST support authenticated negotiation of an application protocol.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow CRYPTO frames in multiple packet number spaces
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The CRYPTO frame MAY be sent in different packet number spaces.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Permit application data exchange after handshake completion
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once the handshake is complete, endpoints MUST be able to exchange application data.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use the cryptographic handshake after address validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once any address validation exchanges are complete, the cryptographic handshake MUST be used to agree on cryptographic keys.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Carry the cryptographic handshake in Initial and Handshake packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST be carried in Initial and Handshake packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Coalesce multiple QUIC packets into one UDP datagram
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Multiple QUIC packets, even of different packet types, MAY be coalesced into a single UDP datagram.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Client sends 1-RTT packets in the same packet number space
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The client MUST send 1-RTT packets in the same packet number space.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Server acknowledges 0-RTT data in 1-RTT packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The server MUST acknowledge 0-RTT data in 1-RTT packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Destination Connection ID provides consistent routing
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Destination Connection ID MUST be used to provide consistent routing of packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Long header contains two connection IDs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The long header MUST contain two connection IDs.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Recipient chooses the Destination Connection ID
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The recipient of the packet MUST choose the Destination Connection ID.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Source Connection ID sets the peer Destination Connection ID
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Source Connection ID MUST be used to set the Destination Connection ID used by the peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Source Connection ID specifies destination connection ID
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each endpoint MUST use the Source Connection ID field to specify the connection ID used in the Destination Connection ID field of packets being sent to it.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Client uses an unpredictable destination connection ID before server contact
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When an Initial packet is sent by a client that has not previously received an Initial or Retry packet from the server, the client MUST populate the Destination Connection ID field with an unpredictable value.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use first Initial DCID to determine Initial packet keys
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Destination Connection ID field from the first Initial packet sent by a client MUST be used to determine packet protection keys for Initial packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Change Initial packet keys after Retry
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packet protection keys for Initial packets MUST change after receiving a Retry packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Populate Source Connection ID with a client-chosen value
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The client MUST populate the Source Connection ID field with a value of its choosing.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Set Source Connection ID Length to indicate the length
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The client MUST set the Source Connection ID Length field to indicate the length.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Change the destination connection ID only for the first Initial or Retry packet
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client MUST change the Destination Connection ID it uses for sending packets only in response to the first received Initial or Retry packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit later destination connection ID changes to NEW_CONNECTION_ID values
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Any further changes to the Destination Connection ID MUST be taken from NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Authenticate handshake connection IDs through transport parameters
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each endpoint MUST include all connection ID values used during the handshake in transport parameters.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include the first received Initial Destination CID in transport parameters
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST include the Destination Connection ID field from the first Initial packet it received from the client in the original_destination_connection_id transport parameter; if the server sent a Retry packet, this refers to the first Initial packet received before sending the Retry packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include the Retry packet Source CID in transport parameters
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST include the Source Connection ID field from the Retry packet in the retry_source_connection_id transport parameter if it sends a Retry packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Match transport parameter values to the endpoint's Initial packet connection IDs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The values provided by a peer for these transport parameters MUST match the values that an endpoint used in the Destination and Source Connection ID fields of Initial packets that it sent, and for servers, received.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat missing initial_source_connection_id as transport parameter error
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST treat the absence of the initial_source_connection_id transport parameter from either endpoint as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat missing original_destination_connection_id as transport parameter error
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST treat the absence of the original_destination_connection_id transport parameter from the server as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat missing retry_source_connection_id after Retry as connection error
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST treat the absence of the retry_source_connection_id transport parameter from the server after receiving a Retry packet as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR or PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat retry_source_connection_id without Retry as connection error
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST treat the presence of the retry_source_connection_id transport parameter when no Retry packet was received as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR or PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat mismatched Initial packet connection ID values as connection error
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST treat a mismatch between values received from a peer in these transport parameters and the value sent in the corresponding Destination or Source Connection ID fields of Initial packets as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR or PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Validate peer transport parameter values
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST validate the values provided by its peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Apply client handshake transport parameters to all offered application protocols
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The transport parameters that a client includes during the handshake MUST apply to all application protocols that the client offers.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Store server transport parameters with session tickets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MUST store server transport parameter values with any session tickets they receive.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use stored transport parameters when attempting 0-RTT
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MUST use stored transport parameter values when attempting 0-RTT using the session tickets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Apply remembered transport parameters until handshake completion and 1-RTT traffic
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Remembered transport parameters MUST apply to the new connection until the handshake completes and the client starts sending 1-RTT packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use handshake transport parameters after handshake completion
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once the handshake completes, the client MUST use the transport parameters established in the handshake.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Specify 0-RTT storage behavior for new transport parameters
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The definition of a new transport parameter MUST specify whether storing the transport parameter for 0-RTT is mandatory, optional, or prohibited.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Client may omit unprocessable transport parameters
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client MAY omit storing a transport parameter it cannot process.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not use remembered 0-RTT parameter values
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client MUST use handshake values, not remembered values, for ack_delay_exponent, max_ack_delay, initial_source_connection_id, original_destination_connection_id, preferred_address, retry_source_connection_id, and stateless_reset_token.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not lower remembered 0-RTT limit values
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If 0-RTT data is accepted by the server, the server MUST keep active_connection_id_limit, initial_max_data, initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local, initial_max_stream_data_bidi_remote, initial_max_stream_data_uni, initial_max_streams_bidi, and initial_max_streams_uni at or above the remembered values.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Update sending stream flow control after handshake
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once the handshake completes, the client MUST update the flow control limits on all sending streams using the updated values of initial_max_stream_data_bidi_remote and initial_max_stream_data_uni.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not use updated transport parameters in 0-RTT
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client MUST NOT use updated transport parameter values learned from the server's updated transport parameters or from frames received in 1-RTT packets when sending frames in 0-RTT packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Apply handshake-updated transport parameters only to 1-RTT packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Updated transport parameter values from the handshake MUST apply only to 1-RTT packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Keep remembered flow control limits in 0-RTT
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Flow control limits from remembered transport parameters MUST apply to all 0-RTT packets even if the handshake or frames sent in 1-RTT packets increase those values.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Disable optional features when transport parameters are absent
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The absence of a transport parameter MUST disable any optional protocol feature negotiated using that parameter.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard unknown transport parameters and retry 0-RTT later
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client that does not understand a transport parameter MAY discard it and attempt 0-RTT on subsequent connections.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Maintain out-of-order CRYPTO buffer
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Implementations MUST buffer at least 4096 bytes of out-of-order CRYPTO data.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow larger handshake CRYPTO buffers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MAY buffer more data during the handshake.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow buffer size to vary during connection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint's buffer size MAY change during the life of the connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Temporarily expand handshake buffer
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If an endpoint's buffer is exceeded during the handshake, it MAY temporarily expand its buffer to complete the handshake.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Close when post-handshake CRYPTO buffering is exceeded
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once the handshake completes, if an endpoint cannot buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame, it MAY close the connection with CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard excess post-handshake CRYPTO frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once the handshake completes, if an endpoint cannot buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame, it MAY discard that CRYPTO frame and future CRYPTO frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Acknowledge packets containing discarded CRYPTO frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets containing discarded CRYPTO frames MUST be acknowledged.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit sends to unvalidated addresses
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST limit the data it sends to an unvalidated address to three times the data received from that address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat Handshake-keyed packets as Initial confirmation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a packet protected with Handshake keys as confirmation that the peer successfully processed an Initial packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow validation after Handshake packet processing
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY consider the peer address validated once it has successfully processed a Handshake packet from the peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow validation with high-entropy endpoint-chosen CID
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY consider the peer address validated if the peer uses a connection ID chosen by the endpoint and the connection ID contains at least 64 bits of entropy.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use first Initial DCID for server validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: For a client, the value of the Destination Connection ID field in its first Initial packet MUST allow it to validate the server address as part of successfully processing any packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit server amplification before address validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Prior to validating the client address, servers MUST NOT send more than three times the payload bytes received in datagrams uniquely attributed to a single connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send PTO packet based on handshake-key availability
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: On a PTO, a client MUST send an Initial packet in a UDP datagram containing at least 1200 bytes if it does not have Handshake keys, and a Handshake packet otherwise.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use an Initial-packet token for address validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: QUIC MUST use a token in the Initial packet to provide address validation prior to completing the handshake.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Deliver validation token via Retry or NEW_TOKEN
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A token MUST be delivered to the client during connection establishment with a Retry packet or in a previous connection using the NEW_TOKEN frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Apply congestion controller send limits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Servers MUST be constrained in what they can send by the limits set by the congestion controller.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Client constrained only by congestion controller
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Clients MUST be constrained only by the congestion controller.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Request address validation with Retry
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MAY request address validation by sending a Retry packet with a token.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Repeat Retry token in Initial packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The client MUST repeat the Retry token in all Initial packets for that connection after receiving Retry.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not send another Retry after retry token
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST NOT send another Retry packet after processing an Initial packet containing a Retry token.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Refuse or permit after retry token
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If a server processes an Initial packet containing a Retry token, it MUST either refuse the connection or permit it to proceed.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use Retry to defer connection-establishment costs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MAY use a Retry packet to defer state and processing costs of connection establishment.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Close invalid Retry token connections
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server SHOULD immediately close the connection with an INVALID_TOKEN error.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Avoid closing period without connection state
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST NOT enter the closing period before establishing any connection state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Provide address validation tokens
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MAY provide a client with an address validation token for use on a subsequent connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use NEW_TOKEN for validation tokens
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST use the NEW_TOKEN frame to provide an address validation token for future connections.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include future-connection token in Initial packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The client MUST include the token in every Initial packet it sends, unless Retry replaces it with a newer token.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Give NEW_TOKEN tokens an expiration time
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A token SHOULD have an expiration time, explicit or derivable from an issued timestamp.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Prevent linkable information in NEW_TOKEN tokens
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A token issued with NEW_TOKEN MUST NOT include information that would let an observer link it to the connection on which it was issued.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Keep NEW_TOKEN frames unique across clients
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST ensure that every NEW_TOKEN frame it sends is unique across all clients, except frames sent to repair loss of previously sent NEW_TOKEN frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Token-disambiguation information may be accessible externally
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Information that lets the server distinguish Retry tokens from NEW_TOKEN tokens MAY be accessible to other entities.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: NEW_TOKEN tokens apply to authoritative servers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A token received in a NEW_TOKEN frame MUST be applicable to any server the connection is authoritative for.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not send tokens to non-applicable servers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client MUST NOT include a token that is not applicable to the server it is connecting to, unless it knows the issuing server and target server jointly manage the tokens.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not reuse Retry tokens in later attempts
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A token obtained in a Retry packet MUST NOT be used in subsequent connection attempts.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use Retry tokens immediately
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A token obtained in a Retry packet MUST be used immediately during the connection attempt.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not reuse NEW_TOKEN tokens across attempts
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client SHOULD NOT reuse a token from a NEW_TOKEN frame across different connection attempts.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reuse tokens across same-version connection attempts
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Clients MAY use a token obtained on one connection for any same-version connection attempt.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ignore unrelated connection properties when selecting a token
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When selecting a token to use, clients MAY ignore application protocols, session tickets, and other properties of the attempted connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Protect tokens from client modification or falsification
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The token MUST be covered by integrity protection against modification or falsification by clients.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow NEW_TOKEN tokens to suppress Retry
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Servers MAY use tokens from NEW_TOKEN frames in deciding not to send a Retry packet, even if the client address has changed.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Prevent or limit token replay
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Servers MUST ensure that replay of tokens is prevented or limited.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit Retry token acceptance lifetime
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Servers SHOULD ensure that tokens sent in Retry packets are only accepted for a short time.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reject repeated acceptance of NEW_TOKEN tokens
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Tokens in NEW_TOKEN frames SHOULD NOT be accepted multiple times.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow client-specific token data
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Tokens MAY include additional information about clients to further narrow applicability or reuse.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Prefer single-use tokens when possible
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Servers SHOULD allow tokens to be used only once, if possible.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Test reachability between specific addresses
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In path validation, endpoints MUST test reachability between a specific local address and a specific peer address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Confirm packets on a path are received by the peer
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Path validation MUST test that packets sent on a path to a peer are received by that peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Prevent spoofed source addresses during migration
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Path validation MUST ensure that packets received from a migrating peer do not carry a spoofed source address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not validate return-direction sendability
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Path validation MUST NOT validate that a peer can send in the return direction.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not use acknowledgments for return path validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: ACKs MUST NOT be used for return path validation.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Determine reachability independently per path direction
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MUST independently determine reachability for each direction of a path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow path validation at any time
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Path validation MAY be used at any time by either endpoint.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow PADDING with PATH_CHALLENGE for PMTUD
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY include PADDING frames with a PATH_CHALLENGE frame for Path Maximum Transmission Unit Discovery (PMTUD).

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow PATH_CHALLENGE with PATH_RESPONSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY include its own PATH_CHALLENGE frame when sending a PATH_RESPONSE frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use a new connection ID for probes from a new local address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST use a new connection ID for probes sent from a new local address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send NEW_CONNECTION_ID and PATH_CHALLENGE together when permitted
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the peer's active_connection_id_limit permits, an endpoint MAY send NEW_CONNECTION_ID and PATH_CHALLENGE frames in the same packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow simultaneous probing of multiple paths
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY simultaneously probe multiple paths.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit simultaneous probe paths by available connection IDs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The number of simultaneous paths used for probes MUST be limited by the number of extra connection IDs previously supplied by the peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Initiate path validation with PATH_CHALLENGE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST send a PATH_CHALLENGE frame on the path to be validated.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Avoid multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames per packet
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD NOT send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in a single packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use unpredictable PATH_CHALLENGE payloads
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The endpoint MUST use unpredictable data in every PATH_CHALLENGE frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Expand PATH_CHALLENGE datagrams to 1200 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Datagrams containing PATH_CHALLENGE MUST be at least 1200 bytes unless anti-amplification limits prevent that.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not validate path MTU when expansion is blocked
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If anti-amplification limits prevent expanding a datagram to 1200 bytes, the path MTU MUST NOT be validated.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Perform second path validation with PATH_CHALLENGE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The endpoint MUST perform a second path validation by sending a PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a datagram of at least 1200 bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retain datagrams carrying PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MUST NOT discard datagrams that contain PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE just because they appear too small.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Echo PATH_CHALLENGE data in PATH_RESPONSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST echo the PATH_CHALLENGE data in a PATH_RESPONSE frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send PATH_RESPONSE without delay unless congested
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT delay transmission of a PATH_RESPONSE frame unless congestion control constrains it.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not enforce received-path response requirement during initiation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The endpoint that initiates path validation MUST NOT require a PATH_RESPONSE frame to be sent on the network path where the PATH_CHALLENGE frame was received.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Expand PATH_RESPONSE datagrams to 1200 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST expand datagrams containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame to at least 1200 bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not expand PATH_RESPONSE datagrams beyond the anti-amplification limit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT expand the datagram containing the PATH_RESPONSE if the resulting data exceeds the anti-amplification limit.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Validate matching PATH_RESPONSE data
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A PATH_RESPONSE frame containing data from a previous PATH_CHALLENGE MUST validate the path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Let any valid PATH_RESPONSE confirm the challenged path
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A PATH_RESPONSE frame received on any network path MUST validate the path on which the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE was sent.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat undersized challenged datagrams as validating only the path
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If an endpoint sends a PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a datagram not expanded to at least 1200 bytes and the response validates the peer address, the path MUST be validated, but the path MTU is not validated.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retry path validation with an expanded datagram for MTU checks
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The endpoint MUST initiate another path validation with an expanded datagram to verify that the path supports the required MTU.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not validate path based on ACKs for PATH_CHALLENGE packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Receipt of an acknowledgment for a packet containing a PATH_CHALLENGE frame MUST NOT be treated as adequate validation.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Fail path validation only when validation is abandoned
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Path validation MUST NOT fail unless the endpoint attempting to validate the path abandons its attempt to validate the path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Timer value for failed path validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An implementation SHOULD set the timer to three times the larger of the current PTO or the PTO for the new path, using kInitialRtt as defined in [QUIC-RECOVERY].

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Path validation requires a PATH_RESPONSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Path validation MUST succeed only when a PATH_RESPONSE frame with appropriate data is received.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Abandoned path validation marks the path unusable
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When an endpoint abandons path validation, it MUST consider the path unusable.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: No available paths
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If no paths are available, an endpoint MAY wait for a new path to become available or close the connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: NO_VIABLE_PATH signaling
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that has no valid network path to its peer MAY signal this using the NO_VIABLE_PATH connection error, but only if the network path exists and does not support the required MTU.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Respect disable_active_migration when sending packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the peer sent the disable_active_migration transport parameter, an endpoint MUST not send packets, including probing packets, from a different local address to the address the peer used during the handshake, unless the endpoint has acted on a preferred_address transport parameter from the peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Clients initiate connection migration
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Except as described in Section 9.6, clients MUST initiate all connection migrations.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Probe new local addresses before migration
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY probe for peer reachability from a new local address using path validation (Section 8.2) before migrating the connection to that address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Failed path validation leaves the path unusable
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If path validation fails, the new path MUST NOT be usable for this connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Path validation failure does not end the connection by itself
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Failure to validate a path MUST NOT end the connection unless no valid alternative paths are available.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Classify only probing-frame packets as probing packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A packet containing only probing frames MUST be classified as a probing packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Classify packets with any other frame as non-probing packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A packet containing any other frame MUST be classified as a non-probing packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Migrate by sending non-probing frames from the new local address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY migrate a connection to a new local address by sending non-probing frames from that address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reset congestion control and RTT estimate on migration
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When migrating, the endpoint MUST reset its congestion controller and RTT estimate.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Validate ECN capability on migration
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When migrating, the endpoint MUST validate ECN capability.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat a non-probing frame from a new address as migration
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Receiving a packet from a new peer address that contains a non-probing frame MUST indicate that the peer has migrated to that address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Initiate path validation when migration is permitted
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the recipient permits the migration and validation is not already underway, it MUST initiate path validation (Section 8.2) to verify the peer's ownership of the address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not send on a new path without an unused connection ID
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the recipient has no unused connection IDs from the peer, it MUST NOT send anything on the new path until the peer provides one.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Validate new peer address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST validate a peer's new address to confirm the peer's possession of the new address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit sending to unvalidated peer addresses
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Until a peer's address is valid, an endpoint MUST limit the amount of data it sends to that address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: May refrain from limiting sending rate after skipping validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If an endpoint skips validation of a peer address, it MAY refrain from limiting its sending rate.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: May abandon other path validation after switching the send address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: After changing the address it uses for non-probing packets, an endpoint MAY abandon validation of other addresses.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Drop original packet as duplicate
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The original packet MUST be seen as a duplicate and dropped.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Spoofed packet appears to come from migrating connection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A packet with a spoofed address MUST be seen to come from a migrating connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Fail source address validation after spurious migration
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: After a spurious migration, validation of the source address MUST fail.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Revert to last validated peer address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST revert to using the last validated peer address when validation of a new peer address fails.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Trigger another migration on higher packet numbers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Receipt of packets with higher packet numbers from the legitimate peer address MUST trigger another connection migration.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Abandon spurious migration validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST abandon validation of the spurious migration when it receives packets with higher packet numbers from the legitimate peer address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send Stateless Reset on further packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to any further incoming packets.
