staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard genuine packet as duplicate
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Any genuine packet MUST be discarded as a duplicate.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Succeed with probing packets when the path is viable but no longer desired
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the path is viable but no longer desired, the validation MUST succeed and result only in probing packets being sent on the path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Time out validation when the path is no longer viable
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the path is no longer viable, the validation attempt MUST time out and fail.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Migrate back to the original path when the genuine packet arrives first
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the non-probing packet arrives before any copy made by an attacker, the connection MUST be migrated back to the original path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Exclude old-path packets from congestion control
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets sent on the old path MUST NOT contribute to congestion control for the new path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Exclude old-path packets from RTT estimation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets sent on the old path MUST NOT contribute to RTT estimation for the new path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reset congestion controller on confirmed new address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: On confirming a peer's ownership of its new address, an endpoint MUST reset the congestion controller for the new path to initial values unless the only change in the peer's address is its port number.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reset RTT estimator on confirmed new address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: On confirming a peer's ownership of its new address, an endpoint MUST reset the round-trip time estimator for the new path to initial values unless the only change in the peer's address is its port number.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: May retain congestion control state on port-only change
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the only change in the peer's address is its port number, the endpoint MAY retain its congestion control state instead of reverting to initial values.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: May retain RTT estimate on port-only change
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the only change in the peer's address is its port number, the endpoint MAY retain its round-trip estimate instead of reverting to initial values.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow probe packet exceptions
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sender MAY make exceptions for probe packets so that their loss detection is independent and does not unduly cause the congestion controller to reduce its sending rate.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not make timer more aggressive
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: This timer MUST NOT be more aggressive than described in Section 6.2.1 of [QUIC-RECOVERY].

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Change Destination Connection ID to an unused value
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MAY change the Destination Connection ID they transmit with to a value unused on another path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not reuse a connection ID across multiple destination addresses
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT reuse a connection ID when sending to more than one destination address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Continue using the current connection ID after receiving packets from a new source address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If packets arrive from a new source address with the same Destination Connection ID field value, an endpoint MAY continue using the current connection ID with the new remote address while still sending from the same local address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: No mid-connection migration to a new server address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A QUIC implementation MUST NOT support migrating a connection to a new server address mid-connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard packets from an unexpected new server address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client SHOULD discard packets from a new server address when the client has not initiated migration to that address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Convey preferred address in TLS handshake
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST include the preferred_address transport parameter in the TLS handshake.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Optionally communicate preferred addresses by address family
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Servers MAY communicate a preferred address for each address family (IPv4 and IPv6).

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Construct packets with a previously unused active connection ID
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client MUST construct packets using any previously unused active connection ID from either the preferred_address transport parameter or a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Switch to the new server address after successful path validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: As soon as path validation succeeds, the client SHOULD begin sending future packets to the new server address using the new connection ID and discontinue use of the old server address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Continue using the original address when path validation fails
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If path validation fails, the client MUST continue sending future packets to the server's original IP address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Respond to PATH_CHALLENGE with PATH_RESPONSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If this packet contains a PATH_CHALLENGE frame, the server MUST send a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame as per Section 8.2.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Switch non-probing packets to the preferred address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once the server has completed path validation and received a non-probing packet with a new largest packet number on its preferred address, the server MUST send non-probing packets only from its preferred IP address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Restrict preferred_address validity to the connection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server's preferred_address transport parameter addresses MUST be treated as valid only for the connection in which they are provided.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Prohibit reuse of preferred_address values across connections
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client MUST NOT use preferred_address values for other connections, including resumed connections.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Preferred-address connection IDs are not address-specific
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The connection ID provided in the preferred_address transport parameter MUST NOT be specific to the provided addresses.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Apply IPv6 flow labels when sending IPv6 data
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints that send data using IPv6 SHOULD apply an IPv6 flow label unless the local API does not allow setting IPv6 flow labels.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Minimize flow-label linkability
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The flow label generation MUST minimize linkability with a previously used flow label.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Close idle connections after the minimum timeout
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If a max_idle_timeout is specified by either endpoint, the connection MUST be silently closed and its state discarded when it remains idle for longer than the minimum of the max_idle_timeout values advertised by both endpoints.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Compute effective idle timeout from advertised values
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each endpoint MUST compute its effective max_idle_timeout as the minimum of the two advertised values, or the sole advertised non-zero value if only one endpoint advertises a non-zero value.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Initiate immediate close before abandoning an advertised idle timeout
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If an endpoint advertises max_idle_timeout and abandons the connection before the effective idle timeout, it MUST initiate an immediate close.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Restart idle timer on the first ack-eliciting send after receive
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST also restart its idle timer when sending an ack-eliciting packet if no other ack-eliciting packets have been sent since the last time it received and processed a packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send liveness probes near PTO expiry
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY send a PING or another ack-eliciting frame if the peer could time out soon.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send periodic PINGs while deferring idle timeout
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When an endpoint uses an idle-timeout deferral option, it MAY send PING frames periodically, and each such PING causes the peer to restart its idle timeout period.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: PING packets restart the idle timeout
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Sending a packet containing a PING frame MUST restart the idle timeout for this endpoint if it is the first ack-eliciting packet sent since receiving a packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: PING acknowledgments restart the idle timeout
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The acknowledgment caused by a PING frame MUST restart the idle timeout for the endpoint.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: PING frames elicit acknowledgments
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Sending a PING frame MUST cause the peer to respond with an acknowledgment.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Idle timeout after negotiated silence
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A connection MUST time out if no packets are sent or received for a period longer than the time negotiated using the max_idle_timeout transport parameter.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Close streams and implicitly reset open streams on CONNECTION_CLOSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MUST cause all streams to immediately become closed and implicitly reset any open streams.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter draining state after receiving CONNECTION_CLOSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: After receiving a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, an endpoint MUST enter the draining state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use CONNECTION_CLOSE with application-supplied error code to signal closure
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When QUIC consequently closes the connection, a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with an application-supplied error code MUST be used to signal closure to the peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Persist closing and draining states for three PTO intervals
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The closing and draining states SHOULD persist for at least three times the current PTO interval as defined in [QUIC-RECOVERY].

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: End closing or draining states early when late packets cannot trigger a response
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints that have some alternative means to ensure that late-arriving packets do not induce a response, such as those that are able to close the UDP socket, MAY end the closing or draining states earlier to allow for faster resource recovery.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retain enough information to generate CONNECTION_CLOSE packets in closing state
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In the closing state, an endpoint MUST retain enough information to generate a packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retain enough information to identify connection packets in closing state
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In the closing state, an endpoint MUST retain enough information to identify packets as belonging to the connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard other connection state for a closing connection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY discard all other connection state when its selected connection ID and the QUIC version are sufficient information to identify packets for a closing connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ignore received frames while closing
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that is closing MAY ignore any received frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit closing-state amplification when packet protection keys are discarded
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that discards packet protection keys MUST limit the cumulative size of packets it sends to three times the cumulative size of the packets that are received and attributed to the connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reuse the same packet while closing
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY send the exact same packet in response to any received packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter draining state on CONNECTION_CLOSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST enter the draining state when it receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not send packets while draining
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint in the draining state MUST NOT send any packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow one CONNECTION_CLOSE response before draining
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY send a single packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame before entering the draining state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow draining from closing on CONNECTION_CLOSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint in the closing state MAY enter the draining state when it receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: End draining when closing state would have ended
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If an endpoint enters the draining state from the closing state, it MUST end the draining state when the closing state would have ended.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use highest available packet protection for CONNECTION_CLOSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame using the highest available packet protection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send CONNECTION_CLOSE in 1-RTT after handshake confirmation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: After handshake confirmation, an endpoint MUST send any CONNECTION_CLOSE frames in 1-RTT packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow lower-protection CONNECTION_CLOSE before handshake confirmation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Before handshake confirmation, an endpoint MAY send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame using a lower packet protection level.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send CONNECTION_CLOSE in Handshake and Initial packets when client handshake keys are unknown
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If a server does not know whether the client has Handshake keys, the server SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and Initial packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send CONNECTION_CLOSE in Handshake and 1-RTT packets before handshake confirmation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Before handshake confirmation, an endpoint SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and 1-RTT packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send CONNECTION_CLOSE in Initial packets before handshake confirmation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Before handshake confirmation, a server SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in an Initial packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Clear Reason Phrase when converting to 0x1c
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MUST clear the Reason Phrase field when converting a CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1d to a CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1c in Initial or Handshake packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use APPLICATION_ERROR when converting to 0x1c
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints SHOULD use the APPLICATION_ERROR code when converting a CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1d to a CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1c in Initial or Handshake packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Coalesce CONNECTION_CLOSE frames into one UDP datagram
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: CONNECTION_CLOSE frames sent in multiple packet types MAY be coalesced into a single UDP datagram.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow CONNECTION_CLOSE in Initial packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in an Initial packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard unauthenticated packets instead of immediately closing
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MAY discard packets rather than immediately close when errors are detected in packets that lack authentication.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not enter closing state before establishing state
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that has not established state MUST NOT enter the closing state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: No closing or draining state without connection state
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint with no connection state MUST NOT enter a closing or draining period when sending a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send stateless reset for an unassociated packet
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to a packet it cannot associate with an active connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Stateless reset token size
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stateless reset token MUST be 16 bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: End the connection on Stateless Reset
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A peer that receives a Stateless Reset MUST immediately end the connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Issue stateless reset tokens in NEW_CONNECTION_ID
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST issue a stateless reset token in the Stateless Reset Token field of a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow servers to issue stateless_reset_token during the handshake
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Servers MAY issue a stateless_reset_token transport parameter during the handshake for the connection ID selected during the handshake.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include stateless reset token
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Stateless Reset MUST include a 128-bit Stateless Reset Token.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include unpredictable bits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Stateless Reset MUST include at least 38 bits of Unpredictable Bits.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Set Stateless Reset fixed bits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Stateless Reset MUST have Fixed Bits (2) = 1.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Start with first two header bits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Stateless Reset MUST start with the first two bits of the packet header.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use entire UDP datagram
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Stateless Reset MUST use an entire UDP datagram.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Set remainder bytes to random-like values
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The remainder of the first byte and an arbitrary number of bytes following it SHOULD be set to values that are indistinguishable from random.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Place stateless reset token in last 16 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The last 16 bytes of the datagram MUST contain a stateless reset token.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Appear as a short-header packet to other entities
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: To entities other than its intended recipient, a Stateless Reset MUST appear to be a packet with a short header.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Pad packets beyond the requested connection ID length
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD ensure that all packets it sends are at least 22 bytes longer than the minimum connection ID length that it requests the peer to include in its packets, adding PADDING frames as necessary.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Keep short Stateless Resets one byte shorter
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that sends a Stateless Reset in response to a packet that is 43 bytes or shorter SHOULD send one byte less than the packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Add unpredictable bytes when expansion may be larger
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST add additional unpredictable bytes if it could have negotiated a packet protection scheme with a larger minimum expansion.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Format Stateless Resets as short-header packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MUST send Stateless Resets as short-header packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat packets ending in a valid stateless reset token as Stateless Reset
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST treat any packet ending in a valid stateless reset token as a Stateless Reset.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow Stateless Reset on long-header packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to a long-header packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not derive Stateless Reset DCID from short headers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT set the Destination Connection ID in a Stateless Reset from a packet with a short header.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Generate resets for all supported versions
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that supports multiple versions of QUIC MUST generate a Stateless Reset accepted by peers that support any version it might support or might have supported before losing state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Remember stateless reset tokens for recently sent datagrams
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST remember stateless reset tokens associated with the connection IDs and remote addresses for datagrams it has recently sent.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Exclude unused or retired reset tokens
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When comparing the trailing 16 bytes of a UDP datagram for a potential Stateless Reset, an endpoint MUST NOT include stateless reset tokens associated with connection IDs that are unused or retired.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include reset tokens from NEW_CONNECTION_ID and transport parameters
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When comparing the trailing 16 bytes of a UDP datagram for a potential Stateless Reset, an endpoint MUST include Stateless Reset Token field values from NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames and the server's transport parameters.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Identify stateless reset by remote-address tokens
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The endpoint MUST identify a received datagram as a Stateless Reset by comparing the last 16 bytes of the datagram with all stateless reset tokens associated with the remote address on which the datagram was received.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Optionally compare every inbound datagram
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The endpoint MAY perform the stateless-reset comparison for every inbound datagram.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Skip the check after successful processing
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MAY skip the stateless-reset comparison if any packet from a datagram is successfully processed.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Perform stateless-reset comparison on unassociated or undecryptable first packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The comparison MUST be performed when the first packet in an incoming datagram either cannot be associated with a connection or cannot be decrypted.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not check unused or retired connection IDs for stateless reset tokens
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT check stateless reset tokens associated with connection IDs it has not used or that have been retired.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Compare stateless reset tokens without leaking token value
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MUST perform the comparison without leaking information about the value of the token.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Make stateless reset tokens difficult to guess
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The stateless reset token MUST be difficult to guess.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use a single static key across connections
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY use a pseudorandom function with a static key and the connection ID chosen by the endpoint to generate stateless reset tokens for all connections to the same endpoint.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Truncate stateless reset token output to 16 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The output of this function MUST be truncated to 16 bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Take the connection ID from the received packet
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The connection ID MUST come from the received packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Require a recoverable connection ID length
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST either use the same connection ID length for all connections or encode the length of the connection ID such that it can be recovered without state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Disallow zero-length connection IDs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT provide a zero-length connection ID.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use each stateless reset token once
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stateless reset token MUST be used only once.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not reuse the connection ID and static key combination
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The combination of connection ID and static key MUST NOT be used for another connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Permit comparing new values against prior values
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY compare new values against all previous values.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Permit treating duplicate values as protocol violations
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY treat a duplicate value as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Make stateless resets indistinguishable without the token
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Without the stateless reset token, a Stateless Reset MUST be indistinguishable from a valid packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Keep sent stateless resets smaller than the triggering packet
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST ensure that every Stateless Reset it sends is smaller than the packet that triggered it, unless it maintains state sufficient to prevent looping.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Signal detected errors to the peer
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that detects an error SHOULD signal the error to its peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include the most appropriate error code in the signaling frame
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The most appropriate error code SHOULD be included in the frame that signals the error.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Avoid stateless reset for errors that can use close or reset stream frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stateless reset SHOULD NOT be used for any error that can be signaled with a CONNECTION_CLOSE or RESET_STREAM frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Signal unusable connection errors with CONNECTION_CLOSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Errors that render the connection unusable MUST be signaled using a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Signal transport errors with frame type 0x1c
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Transport errors MUST be carried in the CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with frame type 0x1c.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard invalid Initial packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY discard an invalid Initial packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow Initial packet discard despite required connection errors
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY discard an Initial packet even where this specification otherwise mandates a connection error.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send RESET_STREAM for recoverable single-stream application errors
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY send a RESET_STREAM frame with an appropriate error code when an application-level error affects only one stream and leaves the connection recoverable.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Restrict RESET_STREAM instigation to the application protocol
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: RESET_STREAM MUST be instigated only by the application protocol that uses QUIC.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reserve stream termination to the application protocol
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A stream MUST NOT be terminated except by the application protocol.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Local cancellation uses direct API
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A local instance of the application protocol MUST use a direct API call.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Remote cancellation uses STOP_SENDING
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A remote instance of the application protocol MUST use the STOP_SENDING frame, which triggers an automatic RESET_STREAM.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Long header packet types
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets with the long header MUST be Initial, 0-RTT, Handshake, or Retry.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use long header during connection establishment
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: This version of QUIC MUST use the long packet header during connection establishment.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use version-independent packet for version negotiation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Version negotiation MUST use a version-independent packet with a long header.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use short header after 1-RTT keys are available
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets with the short header MUST be used after a connection is established and 1-RTT keys are available.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Version Negotiation packets are unprotected
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Version Negotiation packets MUST have no cryptographic protection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retry packets use AEAD protection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Retry packets MUST use an AEAD function to protect against accidental modification.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Initial packets use AEAD with visible-value key derivation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Initial packets MUST use an AEAD function whose keys are derived from a value visible on the wire.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Prefer multiple frames in one packet at the same encryption level
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD include multiple frames in a single packet if they are to be sent at the same encryption level.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Keep coalesced packets separate and complete
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Every QUIC packet coalesced into a single UDP datagram MUST be separate and complete.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Acknowledge coalesced packets separately
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The receiver of coalesced QUIC packets MUST separately acknowledge each QUIC packet, as if they were received as the payload of different UDP datagrams.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Process each coalesced packet individually
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The receiver of coalesced QUIC packets MUST individually process each QUIC packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard or buffer on decryption failure
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If decryption fails because the keys are not available or for any other reason, the receiver MAY either discard the packet or buffer it for later processing.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Process remaining packets after decryption failure
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If decryption fails because the keys are not available or for any other reason, the receiver MUST attempt to process the remaining packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retry, Version Negotiation, and short-header packets cannot be coalesced
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Retry packets, Version Negotiation packets, and packets with a short header MUST NOT be followed by other packets in the same UDP datagram.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retry, Version Negotiation, and short-header packets omit Length fields
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Retry packets, Version Negotiation packets, and packets with a short header MUST NOT contain a Length field.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Packet number range
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The packet number MUST be an integer in the range 0 to 2^62-1.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Separate send and receive packet numbers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each endpoint MUST maintain separate packet numbers for sending and receiving.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reduced packet numbers are encoded in 1 to 4 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When present in a long or short header, packet numbers MUST be reduced and encoded in 1 to 4 bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Version Negotiation and Retry packets omit packet numbers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Version Negotiation and Retry packets MUST NOT include a packet number.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Initial packets use the Initial space
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Initial packets MUST be in the Initial space.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Handshake packets use the Handshake space
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Handshake packets MUST be in the Handshake space.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: 0-RTT packets use the application data space
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: 0-RTT packets MUST be in the application data space.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: 1-RTT packets use the application data space
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: 1-RTT packets MUST be in the application data space.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use different protection keys per packet type
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each packet type MUST use different protection keys.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Acknowledge Initial packets only in Initial packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An Initial packet MUST be acknowledged only in an Initial packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send Initial packets with Initial packet protection keys
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An Initial packet MUST use Initial packet protection keys.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Acknowledge Handshake packets only in Handshake packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Handshake packet MUST be acknowledged only in a Handshake packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send Handshake packets at the Handshake encryption level
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Handshake packet MUST be sent at the Handshake encryption level.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Start packet numbers at zero
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packet numbers in each space MUST start at packet number 0.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Permit Stateless Reset after packet-number exhaustion
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the packet number for sending reaches 2^62-1, an endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to further packets that it receives.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Run duplicate suppression after removing packet protection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Duplicate suppression MUST happen after removing packet protection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Represent packet payloads as complete frames after protection removal
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: After removing packet protection, the payload of QUIC packets MUST consist of a sequence of complete frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Frames stay within one packet
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Frames MUST fit within a single QUIC packet and not span multiple packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Table 3 frame types respect packet limits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each frame type listed in Table 3 MUST be limited to the packet types indicated in the Pkts column.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Table 3 frame types use listed values
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each frame type listed in Table 3 MUST use the type value shown in the table.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Specific frames carry flags in the Frame Type field
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Frame Type field in ACK, STREAM, MAX_STREAMS, STREAMS_BLOCKED, and CONNECTION_CLOSE frames MUST carry other frame-specific flags.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Restrict Initial and Handshake packets to CONNECTION_CLOSE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Initial or Handshake packets MUST not contain any frame other than a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame of type 0x1c.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Packets marked N are not ack-eliciting
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets containing only frames with this marking MUST NOT be ack-eliciting.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Exclude C-marked packets from bytes in flight
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets containing only frames with this marking MUST NOT count toward bytes in flight for congestion control purposes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Packets marked P can probe new paths
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets containing only frames with this marking MAY be used to probe new network paths during connection migration.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Frames marked F are flow controlled
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The contents of frames with this marking MUST be flow controlled.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat unknown frame types as FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST treat the receipt of a frame of unknown type as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Make valid frames idempotent
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A valid frame MUST NOT cause undesirable side effects or errors when received more than once.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Longer encodings may be treated as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY treat the receipt of a frame type that uses a longer encoding than necessary as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: QUIC-layer CONNECTION_CLOSE frames allowed in any packet number space
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: CONNECTION_CLOSE frames signaling errors at the QUIC layer (type 0x1c) MAY appear in any packet number space.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Application-error CONNECTION_CLOSE frames limited to application data packet number space
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: CONNECTION_CLOSE frames signaling application errors (type 0x1d) MUST only appear in the application data packet number space.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: ACK frames allowed in any packet number space
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: ACK frames MAY appear in any packet number space.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: ACK frames only acknowledge packets from the same packet number space
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: ACK frames MUST only acknowledge packets that appeared in the same packet number space.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Servers may treat receipt of prohibited 0-RTT frames as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MAY treat receipt of ACK, CRYPTO, HANDSHAKE_DONE, NEW_TOKEN, PATH_RESPONSE, or RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames in 0-RTT packets as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Require at least one frame per packet
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sender MUST send at least one frame in each QUIC packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Wait briefly to collect frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sender MAY wait briefly to collect multiple frames before sending a packet that is not maximally packed.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use heuristics to choose wait time
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An implementation MAY use heuristics or application sending behavior to decide whether and how long to wait.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Interleave STREAM frames for multiplexing
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Stream multiplexing MUST be achieved by interleaving STREAM frames from multiple streams into QUIC packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow multiple STREAM frames per packet
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A single QUIC packet MAY include multiple STREAM frames from one or more streams.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Block only streams carried in the lost packet
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When a packet loss occurs, only streams with data in that packet MUST be blocked waiting for a retransmission to be received, while other streams can continue making progress.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enqueue STREAM data for application receipt
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: For STREAM frames, data MUST be enqueued in preparation to be received by the application protocol; delivery and consumption are not required.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Acknowledge fully processed packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once a packet has been fully processed, a receiver MUST acknowledge receipt by sending one or more ACK frames containing the packet number of the received packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit delayed ACKs to ack-eliciting packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST send an ACK frame within the maximum ack delay only in response to ack-eliciting packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Only acknowledge non-ack-eliciting packets for other ACKs
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets that are not ack-eliciting MUST be acknowledged only when an ACK frame is sent for other reasons.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Acknowledge ack-eliciting packets within max_ack_delay
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Ack-eliciting packets MUST be acknowledged at least once within the endpoint's communicated max_ack_delay value.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use peer max_ack_delay for retransmission timeouts
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sender MUST use the receiver's max_ack_delay value to determine timer-based retransmission timeouts.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit ACK-only packet responses
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send more than one packet containing only ACK frames in response to an ack-eliciting packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not send non-ack-eliciting packets in response
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send a non-ack-eliciting packet in response to a non-ack-eliciting packet, even if packet gaps precede the received packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Eventually acknowledge non-ack-eliciting packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST eventually acknowledge non-ack-eliciting packets when it sends an ACK frame in response to other events.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not make all otherwise non-ack-eliciting packets ack-eliciting
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send an ack-eliciting frame in all packets that would otherwise be non-ack-eliciting.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Occasionally add ack-eliciting frames to elicit acknowledgments
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that is only sending non-ack-eliciting packets MAY occasionally add an ack-eliciting frame to those packets to ensure that it receives an acknowledgment.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Generate and send ACK frames without delay on reordered or gap-detected ack-eliciting packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In order to assist loss detection at the sender, an endpoint SHOULD generate and send an ACK frame without delay when it receives an ack-eliciting packet if the received packet has a packet number less than another ack-eliciting packet that has been received, or if the packet has a packet number larger than the highest-numbered ack-eliciting packet that has been received and there are missing packets between that packet and this packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard all ACK ranges
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A receiver MAY discard all ACK Ranges.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retain the largest processed packet number
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A receiver MUST retain the largest packet number that has been successfully processed.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Save Largest Acknowledged when sending ACK frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When a packet containing an ACK frame is sent, the Largest Acknowledged field in that frame MAY be saved.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Stop acknowledging packets at or below a sent Largest Acknowledged value
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When a packet containing an ACK frame is acknowledged, the receiver MAY stop acknowledging packets less than or equal to the Largest Acknowledged field in the sent ACK frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send occasional ack-eliciting frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A receiver MAY send a PING or other small ack-eliciting frame occasionally, such as once per round trip, to elicit an ACK from the peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow at least 1 RTT of reordering without ACK frame loss
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In the absence of ACK frame loss, the ACK-tracking algorithm MUST allow at least 1 RTT of reordering.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Continue making forward progress despite spurious retransmissions
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The sender MUST continue making forward progress.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Measure intentional acknowledgment delays
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST measure the delay intentionally introduced between receiving the packet with the largest packet number and sending an acknowledgment.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Encode acknowledgment delay in ACK Delay
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The endpoint MUST encode the acknowledgment delay in the ACK Delay field of an ACK frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Report large measured acknowledgment delay
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: When the measured acknowledgment delay is larger than max_ack_delay, an endpoint SHOULD report the measured delay.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Acknowledge 0-RTT packets with 1-RTT keys
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets a client sends with 0-RTT packet protection MUST be acknowledged by the server in packets protected by 1-RTT keys.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat PADDING packets as in flight
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets containing PADDING frames MUST be considered to be in flight for congestion control purposes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Only-padding packets consume congestion window
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets containing only PADDING frames MUST consume congestion window.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Only-padding packets do not generate acknowledgments
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets containing only PADDING frames MUST NOT generate acknowledgments that open the congestion window.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send non-padding frames periodically
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sender SHOULD periodically send other frames in addition to PADDING frames to elicit acknowledgments from the receiver.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retransmit lost information
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Information MUST be sent again when a packet containing that information is determined to be lost.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Stop retransmission when acknowledged
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Retransmission MUST cease when a packet containing that information is acknowledged.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard CRYPTO data when keys are discarded
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Data in CRYPTO frames for Initial and Handshake packets MUST be discarded when the corresponding packet number space keys are discarded.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retransmit STREAM data unless reset
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Application data sent in STREAM frames MUST be retransmitted in new STREAM frames until the endpoint has sent a RESET_STREAM for that stream.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: ACK frames carry ack delay
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: ACK frames MUST carry the acknowledgment delay from the largest acknowledged packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: ACK frames carry acknowledgments
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: ACK frames MUST carry the most recent set of acknowledgments.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retransmit RESET_STREAM until completion
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A RESET_STREAM frame MUST be sent until it is acknowledged or until all stream data is acknowledged by the peer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retransmit STOP_SENDING until receiver is done
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A STOP_SENDING frame MUST be sent until the receiving part of the stream enters either a Data Recvd or Reset Recvd state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send current maximum data in MAX_DATA frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST send the current connection maximum data in MAX_DATA frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send current maximum stream data in MAX_STREAM_DATA frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST send the current maximum stream data offset in MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Avoid sending MAX_STREAM_DATA frames too often
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD avoid sending MAX_STREAM_DATA frames too often.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Resend MAX_STREAM_DATA on loss or limit update
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST send an updated value when the packet containing the most recent MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a stream is lost or when the limit is updated.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Stop sending MAX_STREAM_DATA frames in closed states
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD stop sending MAX_STREAM_DATA frames when the receiving part of the stream enters a "Size Known" or "Reset Recvd" state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Avoid sending MAX_STREAMS frames too often
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD avoid sending MAX_STREAMS frames too often.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Resend MAX_STREAMS on loss or limit update
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST send an updated value when a packet containing the most recent MAX_STREAMS frame for a stream type is declared lost or when the limit is updated.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Carry blocked signals in dedicated frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: DATA_BLOCKED, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, and STREAMS_BLOCKED frames MUST carry blocked signals.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Make DATA_BLOCKED connection-scoped
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: DATA_BLOCKED frames MUST have connection scope.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Make STREAMS_BLOCKED type-scoped
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: STREAMS_BLOCKED frames MUST be scoped to a specific stream type.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Make STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED stream-scoped
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames MUST have stream scope.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Retransmit blocked-limit frames only while blocked
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST send a new frame if a packet containing the most recent frame for a scope is lost, but only while the endpoint is blocked on the corresponding limit.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include the blocking limit in blocked frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: These frames MUST always include the limit that is causing blocking at the time they are transmitted.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard retransmission information after reordering delay or memory limit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A sender MAY discard this information after a period of time elapses that adequately allows for reordering, such as a PTO, or based on other events, such as reaching a memory limit.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reduce sending rate in response to reported congestion
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints MUST reduce their sending rate in response to reported congestion.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Determine path ECN support before enabling ECN
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: To enable ECN, a sending QUIC endpoint MUST first determine whether a path supports ECN marking.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Determine peer ECN reporting before enabling ECN
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: To enable ECN, a sending QUIC endpoint MUST first determine whether the peer reports the ECN values in received IP headers.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not report ECN counts without ECN support or field access
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint that does not implement ECN support or does not have access to received ECN fields MUST NOT report ECN counts for packets it receives.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Provide ECN feedback when accessible
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST provide feedback about ECN markings it receives, if those markings are accessible, even when it does not set an ECT field in packets it sends.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Count received ECN codepoints
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An ECN-enabled endpoint MUST access the ECN field of a received IP packet with an ECT(0), ECT(1), or ECN-CE codepoint and increase the corresponding ECT(0), ECT(1), or ECN-CE count.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include ECN counts in subsequent ACK frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: ECN counts MUST be included in subsequent ACK frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Maintain separate acknowledgment state per packet number space
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each packet number space MUST maintain separate acknowledgment state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Maintain separate ECN counts per packet number space
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Each packet number space MUST maintain separate ECN counts.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Disable ECN when validation errors are detected
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST disable the use of ECN on that path if errors are detected.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Validate ECN counts per network path
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST validate the ECN counts for each network path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Detect ECN validation failure from lost ECT-marked packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST monitor whether all packets sent with an ECT codepoint are eventually deemed lost.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Attempt ECN validation on active migration
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST attempt to use ECN and validate this on active connection migration to a new path.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Attempt ECN validation on new connections
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST attempt to use ECN and validate this for each new connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Attempt ECN validation when switching to the preferred address
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST attempt to use ECN and validate this when switching to a server's preferred address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow RFC-defined ECN methods
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Implementations MAY use other methods defined in RFCs.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use ECT(1) counts for ECN validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If an implementation uses the ECT(1) codepoint, it MUST perform ECN validation using the reported ECT(1) counts.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Validate ECN counts before use
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST validate the ECN counts before using them when it receives an ACK frame with ECN counts.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Compare ECN counts against the last successfully processed ACK frame
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST compare newly received counts against those from the last successfully processed ACK frame when validating ECN counts.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Validate ECN count increases against newly acknowledged markings
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST validate any increase in the ECN counts based on the ECN markings applied to packets newly acknowledged in the ACK frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Fail validation when ECN counts are missing
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST fail ECN validation if an ACK frame newly acknowledges a packet sent with ECT(0) or ECT(1) and the corresponding ECN counts are not present in the ACK frame.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Fail validation when ECN count increases are insufficient
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST fail ECN validation if the sum of the increases in ECT(0) and ECN-CE counts is less than the number of newly acknowledged packets originally sent with ECT(0).

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Fail validation when ECT(1) counts are insufficient
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST fail ECN validation if the sum of the increases to ECT(1) and ECN-CE counts is less than the number of newly acknowledged packets sent with an ECT(1) marking.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow ECN counts to exceed acknowledged packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: ECN counts MAY be larger than the total number of packets that are acknowledged.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Fail validation when received ECN counts exceed sent packet counts
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST fail ECN validation if the received total count for either ECT(0) or ECT(1) exceeds the total number of packets sent with the corresponding ECT codepoint.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Disable ECN when validation fails
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If validation fails, the endpoint MUST disable ECN.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow ECN revalidation later in the connection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Even if validation fails, an endpoint MAY revalidate ECN for the same path later in the connection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow continued ECN marking after successful validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Upon successful validation, an endpoint MAY continue to set an ECT codepoint in subsequent packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Disable ECN when validation later fails
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST disable ECN if validation later fails.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Define datagram size as UDP payload size
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The datagram size MUST be the total UDP payload size of a single UDP datagram carrying QUIC packets.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Datagram size excludes UDP and IP headers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The datagram size MUST not include the UDP or IP headers.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Datagram size includes QUIC packet headers and protected payloads
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The datagram size MUST include QUIC packet headers and protected payloads.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Define maximum datagram size by path-supported UDP payload
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The maximum datagram size MUST be the largest size of UDP payload that can be sent across a network path using a single UDP datagram.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Set the IPv4 DF bit when possible
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In IPv4, the Don't Fragment (DF) bit MUST be set if possible.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat datagram size as unauthenticated
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Datagram size MUST not be authenticated.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow discarding datagrams that do not meet size constraints
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY discard such datagrams.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not close connections on invalid datagram sizes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MUST not close a connection when it receives a datagram that does not meet size constraints.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Expand Initial datagrams to 1200 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client MUST expand UDP datagrams carrying Initial packets to at least 1200 bytes by adding PADDING frames to the Initial packet or by coalescing the Initial packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Expand server Initial datagrams to 1200 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST expand UDP datagrams carrying ack-eliciting Initial packets to at least 1200 bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow Initial datagrams above 1200 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Datagrams containing Initial packets MAY exceed 1200 bytes if the sender believes that the network path and peer both support the size it chooses.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard undersized Initial packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST discard an Initial packet carried in a UDP datagram with a payload smaller than 1200 bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow immediate close for undersized Initial packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MAY immediately close the connection by sending a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with an error code of PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit bytes sent before address validation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The server MUST limit the number of bytes it sends before validating the client's address.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use DPLPMTUD or PMTUD to determine path support
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint SHOULD use DPLPMTUD or PMTUD to determine whether the path to a destination supports a desired maximum datagram size without fragmentation.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Avoid oversized datagrams without PMTU discovery
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Without DPLPMTUD or PMTUD, QUIC endpoints SHOULD NOT send datagrams larger than the smallest allowed maximum datagram size.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Size non-probe packets within the maximum datagram size
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: All QUIC packets that are not sent in a PMTU probe SHOULD fit within the maximum datagram size.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Stop sending packets when PMTU cannot support 1200 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If a QUIC endpoint determines that the PMTU between any pair of local and remote IP addresses cannot support 1200 bytes, it MUST immediately cease sending QUIC packets on the affected path, except for PMTU probes and CONNECTION_CLOSE frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Maintain a maximum datagram size per address pair
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: QUIC implementations that perform PMTU discovery SHOULD maintain a maximum datagram size for each local and remote IP address pair.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow a more conservative maximum datagram size computation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A QUIC implementation MAY compute the maximum datagram size more conservatively to allow for unknown tunnel overheads or IP header options or extensions.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Track loss or acknowledgment of PMTU probe packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A DPLPMTUD implementation MUST track loss or acknowledgment of QUIC packets carried in PMTU probes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use PADDING-frame probes as DPLPMTUD probing using padding data
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: PMTU probes for DPLPMTUD that use the PADDING frame MUST implement "Probing using padding data" as defined in Section 4.1 of DPLPMTUD.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Maintain MPS per local and remote IP address pair
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: QUIC endpoints implementing DPLPMTUD MUST maintain a DPLPMTUD Maximum Packet Size (MPS) for each combination of local and remote IP addresses.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Enter DPLPMTUD BASE after handshake completion
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A QUIC sender MAY enter the DPLPMTUD BASE state after the QUIC connection handshake has completed.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not implement CONFIRMATION_TIMER in SEARCH_COMPLETE
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A QUIC sender MUST NOT implement a DPLPMTUD CONFIRMATION_TIMER while in the SEARCH_COMPLETE state.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Validate ICMP PTB before using PTB information
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint using DPLPMTUD MUST validate any received ICMP PTB message before using the PTB information.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Validate ICMP messages with packetization-layer information
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In addition to UDP port validation, QUIC MUST validate an ICMP message by using other packetization-layer information, such as validation of connection IDs in the quoted packet of any received ICMP message.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: PMTU probes are ack-eliciting
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: PMTU probes MUST be ack-eliciting.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not treat PMTU probe loss as congestion
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Loss of a QUIC packet carried in a PMTU probe SHOULD NOT trigger a congestion control reaction.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Consume congestion window for PMTU probes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: PMTU probes MUST consume congestion window.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not acknowledge long header packets after handshake completion
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Long header packets MUST NOT be acknowledged by the peer once the handshake is complete.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Do not decrypt long header packets after handshake completion
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Long header packets MUST NOT be decrypted by the peer once the handshake is complete.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Exclude Source Connection ID from non-long-header packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets other than long header packets MUST NOT contain the Source Connection ID field.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include Source Connection ID in long header packets
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Long header packets MUST contain the Source Connection ID field.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Coalesce long and short header packets into a PMTU probe
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An endpoint MAY construct a PMTU probe by coalescing a long-header packet, such as a Handshake or 0-RTT packet, with a short-header packet in a single UDP datagram.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Acknowledge the short-header packet when a PMTU probe reaches the endpoint
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the resulting PMTU probe reaches the endpoint, the short-header packet MUST be acknowledged.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ignore the long-header packet when a PMTU probe reaches the endpoint
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: If the resulting PMTU probe reaches the endpoint, the long-header packet MUST be ignored.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow PMTU probe packets to be invalid
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A PMTU probe packet MAY be invalid.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Allow PMTU probe packets to be sent without current use
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A PMTU probe packet MAY be sent even if there is no current use for packets of that type.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Smaller values use fewer bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The variable-length integer encoding MUST use fewer bytes for smaller integer values.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use 00 for 1-byte encodings
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A 1-byte encoding MUST use the first two bits `00`, encode 6 usable bits, and cover the range 0-63.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use 01 for 2-byte encodings
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A 2-byte encoding MUST use the first two bits `01`, encode 14 usable bits, and cover the range 0-16383.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use 10 for 4-byte encodings
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A 4-byte encoding MUST use the first two bits `10`, encode 30 usable bits, and cover the range 0-1073741823.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use 11 for 8-byte encodings
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An 8-byte encoding MUST use the first two bits `11`, encode 62 usable bits, and cover the range 0-4611686018427387903.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Encode numeric values in big-endian order
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Numeric values MUST use network byte order (big endian).

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Measure field sizes in bits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Field sizes MUST be measured in bits.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Constrain packet numbers to 62 bits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packet numbers MUST be integers in the range 0 to 2^62-1.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Encode packet numbers in 1 to 4 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packet numbers in long or short packet headers MUST be encoded in 1 to 4 bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use only the least significant packet-number bits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packet number encoding MUST include only the least significant bits of the packet number.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Protect encoded packet numbers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The encoded packet number MUST be protected as described in Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include the full packet number before acknowledgment
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Prior to receiving an acknowledgment for a packet number space, the full packet number MUST be included.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Packet number encoding size lower bound after acknowledgment
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: After an acknowledgment is received for a packet number space, the sender MUST use a packet number size that is at least one bit more than the base-2 logarithm of the number of contiguous unacknowledged packet numbers, including the new packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Remove packet-number protection before recovery
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: At a receiver, protection of the packet number MUST be removed prior to recovering the full packet number.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Reconstruct the full packet number from significant bits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The full packet number MUST be reconstructed based on the number of significant bits present, the value of those bits, and the largest packet number received in a successfully authenticated packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Decode packet number by nearest expected value
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once header protection is removed, the packet number MUST be decoded by finding the packet number value that is closest to the next expected packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Define next expected packet number
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The next expected packet MUST be the highest received packet number plus one.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Encode long-header packet fields
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A long header packet MUST contain, in order, a 2-bit Long Packet Type field, a 4-bit Type-Specific Bits field, a 32-bit Version field, an 8-bit Destination Connection ID Length field, a Destination Connection ID of 0..160 bits, an 8-bit Source Connection ID Length field, a Source Connection ID of 0..160 bits, and a Type-Specific Payload.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Set long-header fixed bit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In a long header packet, the next bit of byte 0 (the Fixed Bit) MUST be 1 unless the packet is a Version Negotiation packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Set long-header form bit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In a long header packet, the most significant bit of byte 0 (the Header Form bit) MUST be 1.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Switch to short header after 1-RTT keys
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Once 1-RTT keys are available, a sender MUST use the short header.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Discard packets with zero fixed bit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Packets containing a zero value for the Fixed Bit MUST be discarded.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Encode long packet type in byte 0
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The next two bits (mask 0x30) of byte 0 MUST contain the packet type.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Interpret type-specific bits by packet type
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The lower four bits (mask 0x0f) of byte 0 MUST be interpreted according to the packet type.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Place QUIC Version after the first byte
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The QUIC Version field MUST be 32 bits and follow byte 0.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Use QUIC Version to interpret protocol fields
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The QUIC Version field MUST determine how the rest of the protocol fields are interpreted.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Encode Destination Connection ID length as 8 bits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Destination Connection ID Length MUST be encoded as an 8-bit unsigned integer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit version 1 Destination Connection ID length to 20 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In QUIC version 1, the Destination Connection ID Length MUST NOT exceed 20 bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Drop version 1 long headers with oversized Destination Connection ID lengths
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints that receive a version 1 long header with a Destination Connection ID Length greater than 20 MUST drop the packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Read longer connection IDs for Version Negotiation
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Servers SHOULD be able to read longer connection IDs from other QUIC versions to form a Version Negotiation packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Encode Source Connection ID length as 8 bits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Source Connection ID Length MUST be encoded as an 8-bit unsigned integer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Limit Source Connection ID Length in version 1
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In QUIC version 1, the Source Connection ID Length MUST NOT exceed 20 bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Drop oversized version 1 long headers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Endpoints that receive a version 1 long header with a Source Connection ID Length field larger than 20 MUST drop the packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Source Connection ID field placement
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Source Connection ID field MUST follow the Source Connection ID Length field.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Treat reserved-bit packets as protocol errors
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: After removing packet and header protection, a packet with non-zero reserved bits MUST be treated as a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION connection error.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Encode packet number length in byte 0
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: In packet types that contain a Packet Number field, the least significant two bits of byte 0 MUST encode that field's length minus one.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Protect packet number length bits
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Packet Number Length bits of byte 0 MUST be protected using header protection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Encode Length as variable-length integer
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Length field MUST be encoded as a variable-length integer.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Length equals remainder of packet
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Length field MUST equal the byte length of the remainder of the packet, including the Packet Number and Payload fields.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Constrain packet number size to 1 to 4 bytes
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Packet Number field MUST be 1 to 4 bytes long.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Protect packet number with header protection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The packet number MUST be protected using header protection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Packet payload contains frames
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Packet Payload MUST contain a sequence of frames.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Protect packet payload with packet protection
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Packet Payload MUST be protected using packet protection.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Keep Version Negotiation packets version independent
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST NOT be version specific.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Identify Version Negotiation packets from Version zero
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A client MUST identify a received packet as a Version Negotiation packet if the Version field has a value of 0.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Send Version Negotiation packets only for unsupported versions
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST send a Version Negotiation packet only in response to a packet that indicates an unsupported version.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Version Negotiation packets are sent only by servers
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Version Negotiation packets MUST be sent only by servers.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Include Supported Version fields
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST include one or more Supported Version fields that are each 32 bits wide.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Preserve the Version Negotiation field order
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST have Header Form, Unused, Version, Destination Connection ID Length, Destination Connection ID, Source Connection ID Length, Source Connection ID, and Supported Version fields in that order.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Set the Header Form bit
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST have Header Form (1) set to 1.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Size the connection ID fields
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST have Destination Connection ID and Source Connection ID fields that are each 0..2040 bytes.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Size the connection ID length fields
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST have Destination Connection ID Length and Source Connection ID Length fields that are 8 bits wide.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Size the Unused field
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST have an Unused field that is 7 bits wide.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Set the Unused field arbitrarily
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A server MUST set the value in the Unused field to an arbitrary value.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Set the Unused field MSB when multiplexing
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Where QUIC might be multiplexed with other protocols, servers SHOULD set the most significant bit of this field (0x40) to 1 so that Version Negotiation packets appear to have the Fixed Bit field.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Copy Source Connection ID from the received Destination Connection ID
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Source Connection ID MUST be copied from the Destination Connection ID of the received packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Ignore version-specific connection ID rules when deciding to send
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: Version-specific rules for the connection ID MUST NOT influence a decision about whether to send a Version Negotiation packet.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Version Negotiation packet carries supported versions list
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The remainder of the Version Negotiation packet MUST be a list of 32-bit versions that the server supports.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Version Negotiation packet omits Length field
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Version Negotiation packet MUST NOT include the Length field present in other packets that use the long header form.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Version Negotiation packet omits Packet Number field
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: The Version Negotiation packet MUST NOT include the Packet Number field present in other packets that use the long header form.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Version Negotiation packet consumes a UDP datagram
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST consume an entire UDP datagram.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Initial packet field layout
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An Initial packet header MUST include the Reserved Bits, Packet Number Length, Version, Destination Connection ID Length, Destination Connection ID, Source Connection ID Length, Source Connection ID, Token Length, Token, Length, Packet Number, and Packet Payload fields in the order shown, with the sizes shown.

staged_ids_not_in_live.title: Initial packet first-byte values
staged_ids_not_in_live.statement: An Initial packet header MUST set Header Form to 1, Fixed Bit to 1, and Long Packet Type to 0.
